title: Birth and rescue of Moses; killing of the Egyptian; flight to Midian; Israel's cry ↔ Pharaoh's oppression and the infant Moses on the water
summary: These two units share 11 motifs: sister offers to find a nurse [divergence between the texts], infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts], who decides that moses be put on the water [divergence between the texts], infant returned to his own mother to nurse [divergence between the texts]….

passages.note: Sister offers to find a nurse [divergence between the texts] (The sister's offer: Exodus has hăʾēlēkh wə-qārāʾtî lākh ʾiššâ mêneqet min hā-ʿIvriyyōt on her own initiative; the Quran first has God forbid the other wet-nurses to him (wa-ḥarramnā ʿalayhi l-marāḍiʿa min qablu), then the sister offers a household that will rear him. cf. b. Sotah 12b (Moses refuses Egyptian breasts), outside the HB.)

passages.note: Infant adopted by a royal woman [divergence between the texts] (Who finds and adopts him: Pharaoh's daughter (bat Parʿōh), bathing, sees the basket, has pity on the crying child, recognizes him as Hebrew (mī-yaldê hā-ʿIvrîm zeh) and later names him. In the Quran Pharaoh's household picks him up (iltaqaṭahu ālu Firʿawn), and Pharaoh's wife (imraʾat Firʿawn) pleads with Pharaoh: qurratu ʿaynin lī wa-laka lā taqtulūhu ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladan. Daughter becomes wife, pity becomes intercession, and the Quran adds the divine irony 'so that he would be an enemy and a grief to them' (28:8).)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Who decides to put the child on the water: Exodus has the mother, on her own, hide him three months and, when she can hide him no longer (wə-lōʾ yākhlâ ʿôd haṣṣəfînô), make a papyrus basket sealed with pitch. In the Quran God inspires her (awḥaynā ilā ummi Mūsā): nurse him, cast him into the river when you fear, and 'we will return him to you and make him one of the messengers'. The rescue is announced in advance. fa-alqīhi fī l-yammi ~ wat-tāśem bas-sûf ʿal śəfat hay-yəʾōr: Exodus places him carefully among the reeds at the edge of the Nile (yəʾōr), in a basket (tēvat gōmeʾ) with bitumen and pitch; the Quran says 'cast him into the yamm', with no vessel in this passage, using the word that elsewhere names the sea where Pharaoh drowns. Who finds and adopts him: Pharaoh's daughter (bat Parʿōh), bathing, sees the basket, has pity on the crying child, recognizes him as Hebrew (mī-yaldê hā-ʿIvrîm zeh) and later names him. In the Quran Pharaoh's household picks him up (iltaqaṭahu ālu Firʿawn), and Pharaoh's wife (imraʾat Firʿawn) pleads with Pharaoh: qurratu ʿaynin lī wa-laka lā taqtulūhu ʿasā an yanfaʿanā aw nattakhidhahu waladan. Daughter becomes wife, pity becomes intercession, and the Quran adds the divine irony 'so that he would be an enemy and a grief to them' (28:8). qālat li-ukhtihi quṣṣīhi fa-baṣurat bihi ʿan junubin wa-hum lā yashʿurūna ~ wat-tētaṣṣav ʾăḥōtô mē-rāḥōq lə-dēʿâ mah yyēʿāśeh lô: the sister watches from a distance. In the Quran the mother sends her. The sister's offer: Exodus has hăʾēlēkh wə-qārāʾtî lākh ʾiššâ mêneqet min hā-ʿIvriyyōt on her own initiative; the Quran first has God forbid the other wet-nurses to him (wa-ḥarramnā ʿalayhi l-marāḍiʿa min qablu), then the sister offers a household that will rear him. cf. b. Sotah 12b (Moses refuses Egyptian breasts), outside the HB. Why the child goes back to his mother: Exodus has a paid arrangement with the princess, hêlîkhî ʾet hay-yeled haz-zeh wə-hênîqihû lî wa-ʾănî ʾettēn ʾet śəkhārēkh; the Quran has God keeping his promise, fa-radadnāhu ilā ummihi kay taqarra ʿaynuhā wa-lā taḥzana wa-li-taʿlama anna waʿda llāhi ḥaqqun. The Quran omits the naming and its etymology (Exod 2:10).

Pair score 62.2.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; Do not take God's name in vain; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; and 3 more.

Only in The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb: The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; Mountain burns with fire to the heart of heaven amid darkness and cloud; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do [response between the texts]; Who was present at the revelation on the mountain, and who knows it only by report [contrast between the texts]; God heard as a voice out of fire with no visible form; The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

title: The Ten Words and the people's fear ↔ Abrogation, the foreign teacher, coerced unbelief, food law, Abraham the hanif and the Sabbath (Surah 16:101-128)
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: the sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts].

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. lōʾ yihyeh-ləkā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy; lā tajʿal maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhar: same first commandment ('other gods' / 'another god'). The frame changes: Exod opens with the exodus, ʾăšer hôṣēʾtîkā mēʾereṣ miṣrayim; Q frames the code with the command at both ends (17:22, 17:39) and with no history of Israel, wa-qaḍā rabbuka. Q's code also has no Sabbath, no images clause and no coveting. kabbēd ʾet-ʾābîkā wəʾet-ʾimmekā ləmaʿan yaʾărikûn yāmêkā; wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan immā yablughanna ʿindaka l-kibara ... fa-lā taqul lahumā uffin ... wa-qul rabbi rḥamhumā ka-mā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. Q drops the promise of long life and puts in its place care for parents in old age and a prayer for them. Duty to parents comes second, right after God, in both. lōʾ tirṣāḥ, unqualified; wa-lā taqtulu n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqq: Q adds 'except by right' and gives the victim's walī authority, fa-lā yusrif fī l-qatl, folding the blood-avenger law into the commandment. lōʾ tinʾāp; wa-lā taqrabū z-zinā innahu kāna fāḥishatan: Q forbids even approaching it, and its zinā covers any illicit intercourse, not only with a married woman.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. A recited list of commandments compared item by item. Kept: no other gods (allā tushrikū bihi shayʾan = lōʾ yihyeh-ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm), parents, killing, sexual sin, false speech. Omitted: the Sabbath (zākhôr ʾet-yôm haš-šabbāt) and coveting; the image ban is folded into 'associate nothing'. Added: allā taqtulū awlādakum min imlāqin, the orphan's property, full measure and weight, keeping God's covenant. The prologue ʾānōkhî YHWH ʾĕlōhêkhā ʾăšer hôṣēʾtîkhā mē-ʾereṣ miṣrayim becomes qul taʿālaw atlu mā ḥarrama rabbukum, without the Exodus.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) (weight 5.4); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.3); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness (weight 5.1). Pair score 34.3.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; Do not take God's name in vain; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; Do not stretch your eyes toward the worldly splendor given to others to test them; and 8 more.

Only in The recited commandments (the Quranic decalogue): List of commandments introduced 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you'; Lest you say scripture was sent only to two groups before us; This is my straight path; follow it and not other ways that scatter you; God gave Moses the book complete and detailing everything; Do not kill your children for fear of poverty; God provides for them and you; Stand firm for justice as witnesses for God even against yourselves, parents and kin, rich or poor; Guardians must keep orphans' property intact and hand it over when they come of age; Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; I set before you life and death, blessing and curse: choose life; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

title: The Ten Words and the people's fear ↔ Tenfold reward; my life and death for God; no bearer bears another's burden
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: whether guilt passes from parents to their descendants [contrast between the texts].

passages.note: Whether guilt passes from parents to their descendants [contrast between the texts] (Two points. (1) Exod: pōqēd ʿăwōn ʾāvōt ʿal-bānîm ʿal-šillēšîm wə-ʿal-ribbēʿîm, guilt carried across generations; Q 6:164 lā taziru wāziratun wizra ukhrā, no one bears another's burden. (2) Both make reward larger than punishment: Exod ʿōśeh ḥesed lā-ʾălāfîm against three or four generations; Q man jāʾa bi-l-ḥasanati fa-lahu ʿashru amthālihā wa-man jāʾa bi-l-sayyiʾati fa-lā yujzā illā mithlahā.)

passages.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת הַמְּנֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ

passages.note: A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark
passages.text: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ כַפֹּ֖רֶת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר אַמָּתַ֤יִם וָחֵ֨צִי֙ אָרְכָּ֔הּ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי רָחְבָּֽהּ

passages.note: A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark
passages.text: וְנָתַתָּ֧ אֶת הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת עַל הָאָרֹ֖ן מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְאֶל הָ֣אָרֹ֔ן תִּתֵּן֙ אֶת הָ֣עֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ

passages.note: A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark
passages.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ כַּפֹּ֖רֶת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר אַמָּתַ֤יִם וָחֵ֨צִי֙ אָרְכָּ֔הּ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי רָחְבָּֽהּ

passages.note: A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups (almond-blossom cups, knobs and flowers; one talent of pure gold)
passages.text: (25:31) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מְנֹרַ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה תֵּעָשֶׂ֤ה הַמְּנוֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ (25:32) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (25:33) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בַּקָּנֶ֥ה הָאֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:34) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (25:35) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:36) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה יִהְי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:37) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱלָה֙ אֶת נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְהֵאִ֖יר עַל עֵ֥בֶר פָּנֶֽיהָ (25:38) וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:39) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

passages.note: A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups
passages.text: (37:17) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת הַמְּנֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ (37:18) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (37:19) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (37:20) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁ֨קָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (37:21) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּֽחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנָּה (37:22) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה הָי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:23) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:24) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל כֵּלֶֽיהָ

passages.note: A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God (lehem panim 'bread of the face' always before me)
passages.text: (25:23) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ שֻׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:24) וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לּ֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:25) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ לּ֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (25:26) וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (25:27) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:28) וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְנִשָּׂא בָ֖ם אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:29) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ קְּעָרֹתָ֜יו וְכַפֹּתָ֗יו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו֙ וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם (25:30) וְנָתַתָּ֧ עַֽל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן לֶ֥חֶם פָּנִ֖ים לְפָנַ֥י תָּמִֽיד

passages.note: A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God
passages.text: (37:10) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:11) וַיְצַ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:12) וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (37:13) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (37:14) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת הָי֖וּ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת בָּתִּים֙ לַבַּדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:15) וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:16) וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶֽת הַכֵּלִ֣ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֗ן אֶת קְעָרֹתָ֤יו וְאֶת כַּפֹּתָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ מְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו וְאֶת הַקְּשָׂוֺ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֖ב טָהֽוֹר

passages.note: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles
passages.text: (25:10) וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:11) וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עָלָ֛יו זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:12) וְיָצַ֣קְתָּ לּ֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וְנָ֣תַתָּ֔ה עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (25:13) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בַדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (25:14) וְהֵֽבֵאתָ֤ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֥את אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן בָּהֶֽם (25:15) בְּטַבְּעֹת֙ הָאָרֹ֔ן יִהְי֖וּ הַבַּדִּ֑ים לֹ֥א יָסֻ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ (25:16) וְנָתַתָּ֖ אֶל הָאָרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ

passages.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ מָסָךְ֙ לְפֶ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֹקֵֽם

passages.note: An embroidered screen at the entrance of the tent or court
passages.text: וְאֶת עַמּוּדָ֤יו חֲמִשָּׁה֙ וְאֶת וָ֣וֵיהֶ֔ם וְצִפָּ֧ה רָאשֵׁיהֶ֛ם וַחֲשֻׁקֵיהֶ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֥ם חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה נְחֹֽשֶׁת

passages.note: Outer coverings of red-dyed ram skins and tahash skins
passages.text: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ מִכְסֶה֙ לָאֹ֔הֶל עֹרֹ֥ת אֵילִ֖ם מְאָדָּמִ֑ים וּמִכְסֵ֛ה עֹרֹ֥ת תְּחָשִׁ֖ים מִלְמָֽעְלָה

passages.note: Outer coverings of red-dyed ram skins and tahash skins
passages.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ מִכְסֶה֙ לָאֹ֔הֶל עֹרֹ֥ת אֵלִ֖ים מְאָדָּמִ֑ים וּמִכְסֵ֛ה עֹרֹ֥ת תְּחָשִׁ֖ים מִלְמָֽעְלָה

passages.note: A middle bar runs through the frames from end to end
passages.text: וְהַבְּרִ֥יחַ הַתִּיכֹ֖ן בְּת֣וֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁ֑ים מַבְרִ֕חַ מִן הַקָּצֶ֖ה אֶל הַקָּצֶֽה

passages.note: A middle bar runs through the frames from end to end
passages.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת הַבְּרִ֣יחַ הַתִּיכֹ֑ן לִבְרֹ֨חַ֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁ֔ים מִן הַקָּצֶ֖ה אֶל הַקָּצֶֽה

passages.note: Curtains joined by fifty loops and fifty clasps (gold clasps on inner curtains, bronze on goat-hair tent)
passages.text: חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת תַּעֲשֶׂה֮ בַּיְרִיעָ֣ה הָאֶחָת֒ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַיְרִיעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּמַּחְבֶּ֣רֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית מַקְבִּילֹת֙ הַלֻּ֣לָאֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל אֲחֹתָֽהּ

passages.note: Curtains joined by fifty loops and fifty clasps (gold clasps on inner curtains, bronze on goat-hair tent)
passages.text: וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים קַרְסֵ֣י זָהָ֑ב וְחִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֶת הַיְרִיעֹ֜ת אִשָּׁ֤ה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ֙ בַּקְּרָסִ֔ים וְהָיָ֥ה הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן אֶחָֽד

passages.note: Curtains joined by fifty loops and fifty clasps
passages.text: חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻלָאֹ֗ת עָשָׂה֮ בַּיְרִיעָ֣ה הָאֶחָת֒ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻלָאֹ֗ת עָשָׂה֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַיְרִיעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּמַּחְבֶּ֣רֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית מַקְבִּילֹת֙ הַלֻּ֣לָאֹ֔ת אַחַ֖ת אֶל אֶחָֽת

passages.note: Curtains joined by fifty loops and fifty clasps
passages.text: וַיַּ֕עַשׂ חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים קַרְסֵ֣י זָהָ֑ב וַיְחַבֵּ֨ר אֶת הַיְרִעֹ֜ת אַחַ֤ת אֶל אַחַת֙ בַּקְּרָסִ֔ים וַֽיְהִ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן אֶחָֽד

passages.note: Tabernacle walls of acacia frames set in silver sockets (two tenons per frame, two silver sockets)
passages.text: (26:15) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים עֹמְדִֽים (26:16) עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:17) שְׁתֵּ֣י יָד֗וֹת לַקֶּ֨רֶשׁ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁלָּבֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל אֲחֹתָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל קַרְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן (26:18) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֶשְׂרִ֣ים קֶ֔רֶשׁ לִפְאַ֖ת נֶ֥גְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה (26:19) וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי כֶ֔סֶף תַּעֲשֶׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו (26:20) וּלְצֶ֧לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית לִפְאַ֣ת צָפ֑וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֖ים קָֽרֶשׁ (26:21) וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:22) וּֽלְיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֥ה קְרָשִֽׁים (26:23) וּשְׁנֵ֤י קְרָשִׁים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לִמְקֻצְעֹ֖ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן בַּיַּרְכָתָֽיִם (26:24) וְיִֽהְי֣וּ תֹֽאֲמִים֮ מִלְּמַטָּה֒ וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ עַל רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַמִּקְצֹעֹ֖ת יִהְיֽוּ (26:25) וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד

passages.note: Tabernacle walls of acacia frames set in silver sockets
passages.text: (36:20) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים עֹמְדִֽים (36:21) עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמֹּ֖ת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (36:22) שְׁתֵּ֣י יָדֹ֗ת לַקֶּ֨רֶשׁ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁלָּבֹ֔ת אַחַ֖ת אֶל אֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֣ן עָשָׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל קַרְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן (36:23) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֶשְׂרִ֣ים קְרָשִׁ֔ים לִפְאַ֖ת נֶ֥גֶב תֵּימָֽנָה (36:24) וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי כֶ֔סֶף עָשָׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקְּרָשִׁ֑ים שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו (36:25) וּלְצֶ֧לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית לִפְאַ֣ת צָפ֑וֹן עָשָׂ֖ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים קְרָשִֽׁים (36:26) וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (36:27) וּֽלְיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה עָשָׂ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֥ה קְרָשִֽׁים (36:28) וּשְׁנֵ֤י קְרָשִׁים֙ עָשָׂ֔ה לִמְקֻצְעֹ֖ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן בַּיַּרְכָתָֽיִם (36:29) וְהָי֣וּ תוֹאֲמִם֮ מִלְּמַטָּה֒ וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ אֶל רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֚ן עָשָׂ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֖י הַמִּקְצֹעֹֽת (36:30) וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֤י אֲדָנִים֙ שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד

passages.note: A veil (parokhet) divides the holy place from the holy of holies
passages.text: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ פָרֹ֗כֶת תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֛ב יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖הּ כְּרֻבִֽים

passages.note: A veil (parokhet) divides the holy place from the holy of holies
passages.text: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֶת הַפָּרֹכֶת֮ תַּ֣חַת הַקְּרָסִים֒ וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ שָׁ֨מָּה֙ מִבֵּ֣ית לַפָּרֹ֔כֶת אֵ֖ת אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵד֑וּת וְהִבְדִּילָ֤ה הַפָּרֹ֨כֶת֙ לָכֶ֔ם בֵּ֣ין הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וּבֵ֖ין קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים

passages.note: A veil (parokhet) divides the holy place from the holy of holies
passages.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת הַפָּרֹ֔כֶת תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֛ב עָשָׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖הּ כְּרֻבִֽים

passages.note: A veil (parokhet) divides the holy place from the holy of holies
passages.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לָ֗הּ אַרְבָּעָה֙ עַמּוּדֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וַיְצַפֵּ֣ם זָהָ֔ב וָוֵיהֶ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וַיִּצֹ֣ק לָהֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעָ֖ה אַדְנֵי כָֽסֶף

passages.note: Tabernacle curtains or veil woven with cherubim
passages.text: וְאֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֥ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה עֶ֣שֶׂר יְרִיעֹ֑ת שֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֗ר וּתְכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י כְּרֻבִ֛ים מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֖ב תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם

passages.note: Tabernacle curtains or veil woven with cherubim
passages.text: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ פָרֹ֗כֶת תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֛ב יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖הּ כְּרֻבִֽים

passages.note: Tabernacle curtains or veil woven with cherubim
passages.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ כָל חֲכַם לֵ֜ב בְּעֹשֵׂ֧י הַמְּלָאכָ֛ה אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן עֶ֣שֶׂר יְרִיעֹ֑ת שֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֗ר וּתְכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י כְּרֻבִ֛ים מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֖ב עָשָׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם

passages.note: Tabernacle curtains or veil woven with cherubim
passages.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת הַפָּרֹ֔כֶת תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֛ב עָשָׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖הּ כְּרֻבִֽים

Only in Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil: The lampstand stands on the south side and the table on the north; The innermost room, the holy of holies, holds the ark; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. miṣbāḥun ... yūqadu min shajaratin mubārakatin zaytūnatin ... yakādu zaytuhā yuḍīʾu ~ šemen zayit zākh kātît la-mmāʾôr ləhaʿălōt nēr tāmîd: a lamp lit with olive oil (zayt / zayit, cognate). In Exodus it is the sanctuary lamp tended by Aaron and his sons from evening to morning; in the Quran it is a parable of God's light, set 'in houses God allowed to be raised' where he is praised morning and evening (24:36).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A perpetual lamp fed with pure beaten olive oil (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Bronze altar, courtyard and lamp oil: Bronze-plated altar of burnt offering with a bronze grating; The altar is hollow, made of boards and carried with poles; The tabernacle court measures 100 by 50 cubits with linen hangings; An altar with horns at its four corners; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in The Light Verse; the mirage, the dark sea, the praising birds, hail and the creatures: Or like darkness in a deep sea, covered by wave upon wave and cloud above, darkness upon darkness, so one cannot see his own hand; The deeds of unbelievers are like a mirage in a plain that the thirsty takes for water until he reaches it and finds nothing, but finds God there; God is the light of the heavens and the earth; God's light is like a niche holding a lamp in a glass like a glittering star, lit from a blessed olive tree neither of east nor west, whose oil almost glows untouched by fire: light upon light; God sends down hail from mountains in the sky; the flash of his lightning nearly takes away sight; In houses God allowed to be raised, men undistracted by trade glorify him morning and evening; God created every beast from water: some go on their bellies, some on two legs, some on four; Birds with outspread wings glorify God; each knows its prayer and praise; With God is the fountain of life; in his light we see light; A lamp fed directly by an olive tree [divergence between the texts]; A golden lampstand with seven lamps is flanked by two olive trees that pour golden oil through golden pipes; The mirage and the thirsty traveler [divergence between the texts]; and 8 more.

passages.text: (39:22) וַיַּ֛עַשׂ אֶת מְעִ֥יל הָאֵפֹ֖ד מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֹרֵ֑ג כְּלִ֖יל תְּכֵֽלֶת (39:23) וּפִֽי הַמְּעִ֥יל בְּתוֹכ֖וֹ כְּפִ֣י תַחְרָ֑א שָׂפָ֥ה לְפִ֛יו סָבִ֖יב לֹ֥א יִקָּרֵֽעַ (39:24) וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ עַל שׁוּלֵ֣י הַמְּעִ֔יל רִמּוֹנֵ֕י תְּכֵ֥לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֖ן וְתוֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֑י מָשְׁזָֽר (39:25) וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ פַעֲמֹנֵ֖י זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ אֶת הַפַּֽעֲמֹנִ֜ים בְּת֣וֹךְ הָרִמֹּנִ֗ים עַל שׁוּלֵ֤י הַמְּעִיל֙ סָבִ֔יב בְּת֖וֹךְ הָרִמֹּנִֽים (39:26) פַּעֲמֹ֤ן וְרִמֹּן֙ פַּעֲמֹ֣ן וְרִמֹּ֔ן עַל שׁוּלֵ֥י הַמְּעִ֖יל סָבִ֑יב לְשָׁרֵ֕ת כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת מֹשֶֽׁה

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The names of the twelve tribes are engraved like seals on gemstones (weight 6.7); The robe's neck opening is bound so it will not tear (weight 6.7); The priest carries Israel's names before God as a memorial (weight 6.7); The priest's robe has gold bells and pomegranates on its hem so he does not die (weight 6.7); The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces (weight 6.3); The breastpiece of judgment set with twelve gems in four rows (weight 6.3); Priests wear linen breeches to cover their nakedness, on pain of death (weight 6.3); A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead (weight 6.0). Pair score 51.6.

Only in The high priest's vestments: Aaron and his sons are designated as priests; Priestly garments are made for glory and beauty; Priests are installed by anointing and 'filling the hand'; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

Only in The vestments made; the work completed and blessed: Gold is beaten into sheets and cut into threads for weaving; The leader sees the finished work and blesses the workers; Completion of the sanctuary is narrated in the language of the completion of creation; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Anointing oil is poured on the head of the priest (weight 6.7); Blood and anointing oil are sprinkled on the priests and their garments (weight 6.7); Ordination of priests lasts seven days (weight 6.7); Portions are waved before God as a wave offering (weight 6.3); Priests are washed with water at the entrance before ordination (weight 6.3); Blood is daubed on the right earlobe, thumb and big toe (weight 6.3); Sacred meat left over until morning is burned (weight 6.3); The offerer lays his hand on the head of the animal (weight 5.8); The flesh, skin and dung of the sin offering are burned outside the camp (weight 5.8); Blood is put on the horns of the altar with the finger and poured at its base (weight 5.8). Pair score 62.5.

Only in Ordination of the priests: A basket of unleavened bread, oiled cakes and wafers is offered; An outsider may not eat holy food; The high priest's vestments pass to his successor, who wears them seven days; The breast and the right thigh are the priests' portion; Sacrificial animals must be without blemish; Whatever touches the most holy altar or holy things becomes holy; An offering by fire is a pleasing odor to God; The fat, the two kidneys and the lobe of the liver are burned on the altar; The fat tail of the sheep is offered.

Only in Moses ordains Aaron and his sons: Moses himself performs the priestly rites at the ordination; The whole congregation is assembled at the tent entrance to witness a rite; Anointing makes the tent and its furnishings holy; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead; A ritual action is performed seven times.

Only in Moses, Ishmael and Idris remembered; the later generation that neglected prayer (Surah 19:51-65): The angels say 'We descend only by your Lord's command'; God has no namesake or equal (samiyy); Ishmael was true to his promise and enjoined prayer and alms on his family; When the Merciful's verses are recited the prophets fall prostrate and weeping; In paradise the blessed receive their provision morning and evening; God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds; A prophet named Idrīs is mentioned among the righteous; God raised Idris to a high place; After the prophets came a generation that neglected prayer and followed lusts; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); The covenant appointment is at the right (ayman) side of the Mount (al-Ṭūr); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him [divergence between the texts]; and 5 more.

Exod 3:15 YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăbōtêkem ʾĕlōhê ʾabrāhām ʾĕlōhê yiṣḥāq wē-ʾlōhê yaʿăqōb: the God of the fathers, three names; Q 2:133 naʿbudu ilāhaka wa-ilāha ābāʾika ibrāhīma wa-ismāʿīla wa-isḥāqa ilāhan wāḥidan: the sons' confession counts Ishmael among Jacob's fathers (properly his uncle), before Isaac.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God identifies himself as God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (weight 5.6). Pair score 12.3.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh; Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Formulaic list of the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite and Jebusite; and 16 more.

Only in Abraham, Ishmael and the House: Abraham and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House while praying; Abraham told 'Submit' answers 'I submit to the Lord of the worlds' (aslamtu); God tests Abraham with words, he fulfills them and is made an imam for mankind; the covenant excludes the wrongdoers among his seed; The 'dye' or baptism (sibgha) of God: who has a better dye than God?; That was a community that has passed; it has what it earned and you what you earned; Dying Jacob asks his sons 'What will you worship after me?' and they confess the God of their fathers; Abraham and Ishmael pray that a messenger be raised from among their offspring; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; Whether and how God's covenant with Abraham passes to his offspring [contrast between the texts]; Whether Ishmael is with Abraham or sent away [contrast between the texts]; Dying Jacob addresses his sons [divergence between the texts]; A nation descended from Ishmael [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. The divine title before Pharaoh: YHWH ʾĕlōhê hā-ʿivriyyîm niqrâ ʿālênû (Exod 3:18, also 5:3) ~ innā rasūlu rabbi l-ʿālamīna, and when Pharaoh asks 'and what is the Lord of the worlds?', Moses answers rabbu s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi wa-mā baynahumā ... rabbu l-mashriqi wa-l-maghribi. The god of one people becomes the Lord of the cosmos. 'God of your fathers' changes addressee. Exod 3:15, said to Israel: YHWH ʾĕlōhê ʾăvōtêkem ʾĕlōhê ʾAvrāhām ʾĕlōhê Yiṣḥāq wē-ʾlōhê Yaʿăqōv. Q 26:26, said to Pharaoh and his court: rabbukum wa-rabbu ābāʾikumu l-awwalīna, 'your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers'. The God of Israel's ancestors becomes the Lord of the Egyptians' ancestors too. Exod 3:18 nēlăkhâ nāʾ derekh šəlōšet yāmîm ba-mmidbār wə-nizbəḥâ la-YHWH ʾĕlōhênû, a request for a three days' journey to sacrifice; Q 26:17 an arsil maʿanā banī Isrāʾīla, an outright demand to release Israel, with no festival, sacrifice or journey of three days.

Shared motifs, rarest first: What Moses asks Pharaoh to allow [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The title of God in whose name Moses goes to Pharaoh (weight 6.7); Whose forefathers' God is proclaimed in the Moses story [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The departing slaves ask their neighbors for silver, gold and clothing and so plunder their oppressors (weight 5.8); God identifies himself as God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (weight 5.6). Pair score 31.4.

Only in The burning bush and the divine name: God names himself 'I will be what I will be' (ehyeh asher ehyeh); God has seen the affliction, heard the cry and comes down to deliver; God introduced to a foreign king as 'the God of the Hebrews'; God foretells that the king will not let the people go except under compulsion; Hero hides his face, afraid to look at God; The sign confirming the call is that the people will later worship on this mountain; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; God declares his name as his everlasting memorial for all generations; The list of fathers in 'God of your fathers' [divergence between the texts]; How God names himself to Moses from the fire [divergence between the texts]; Formulaic list of the Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Perizzite, Hivite and Jebusite; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy) [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Moses and Pharaoh disputing; the magicians; the sea split like mountains: Pharaoh calls the Israelites 'a small band' who enrage him; God expelled the Egyptians from gardens, springs, treasures and fine dwellings and made Israel inherit them; The magicians cast their spells swearing 'By the might of Pharaoh'; Moses admits he did the killing while he was 'of those astray' and fled out of fear; Pharaoh reproaches Moses: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you did your deed?'; Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses if he takes a god other than Pharaoh; Before Pharaoh the staff becomes a manifest great serpent (thuʿbān); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest [divergence between the texts]; Egypt reduced the Israelites to slavery; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; The king musters his whole force to pursue the departing people; How the sea was split for the crossing [divergence between the texts]; and 38 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. innī ānastu nāran ... fa-lammā jāʾahā nūdiya an būrika man fī n-nāri wa-man ḥawlahā ~ wa-yyērāʾ malʾakh YHWH ʾēlāyw bə-labbat ʾēš mit-tôkh has-səneh ... wa-yyiqrāʾ ʾēlāyw ʾĕlōhîm mit-tôkh has-səneh: Moses approaches a fire and is called from within it. The Quran does not mention the bush (only 'who is in the fire and around it'), nor the bush not being consumed. Why Moses goes to the fire: Exodus has him alone with Jethro's flock at Horeb, turning aside to see the great sight (ʾāsurâ nāʾ wə-ʾerʾeh ʾet ham-marʾeh hag-gādōl haz-zeh); the Quran has him traveling with his family (qāla Mūsā li-ahlihi), going to bring back news or a burning brand 'that you may warm yourselves'. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo. The calf as if alive: ʿijlan jasadan lahu khuwārun (a body that lows) vs Aaron's wāʾašlikēhû bāʾēš wayyēṣēʾ hāʿēgel hazzeh ('I threw it in the fire and out came this calf'). cf. Pirqe de-R. Eliezer 45 (the calf comes out lowing), outside the canon. Moses returns angry: rajaʿa ... ghaḍbāna asifan; wa-alqā l-alwāḥa vs wayyiḥar ʾap mōšeh wayyašlēk miyyādāw ʾet-hallūḥōt wayšabbēr ʾōtām taḥat hāhār. Q has only 'cast down' (alqā), never 'broke' (Hebrew šibbēr). Moses confronts Aaron, who blames the people: qāla bna umma inna l-qawma staḍʿafūnī wa-kādū yaqtulūnanī vs ʾal-yiḥar ʾap ʾădōnî ʾattāh yādaʿtā ʾet-hāʿām kî bᵉraʿ hûʾ. Changed: in Exod Aaron made the calf and admits throwing the gold into the fire; in Q he is not its maker and pleads that he was overpowered and nearly killed. He also calls Moses 'son of my mother' instead of ʾădōnî 'my lord'; Q adds the violence (akhadha bi-raʾsi akhīhi yajurruhu ilayhi). Punishment for the calf: sa-yanāluhum ghaḍabun min rabbihim wa-dhillatun fī l-ḥayāti d-dunyā vs the Levites' killing of about 3,000 (kišlōšet ʾalpê ʾîš), the deferred visitation (ûbᵉyôm poqdî ûpāqadtî) and the plague (wayyiggōp YHWH ʾet-hāʿām). Q leaves out the Levite slaughter and gives wrath and humiliation in this life. Moses joins himself to the guilty: in Exod in punishment (wᵉʾim-ʾayin mᵉḥēnî nāʾ missiprᵉkā), answered by mî ʾăšer ḥāṭāʾ-lî ʾemḥennû missiprî; in Q in forgiveness (ighfir lī wa-li-akhī; fa-ghfir lanā wa-rḥamnā), answered by inna rabbaka min baʿdihā la-ghafūrun raḥīm for those who repent.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo, parallel. Same causative of r-ʾ-y in the request: rabbi arinī anẓur ilayka vs harʾēnî nāʾ ʾet-kᵉbōdekā. Moses asks to look at God himself in Q, at his glory (kābôd) in Exod. The refusal, with the same verb and first-person object: lan tarānī vs lōʾ tûkal lirʾōt ʾet-pānāy kî lōʾ-yirʾanî hāʾādām wāḥāy. After the refusal God points Moses to the rock or mountain: wa-lākini nẓur ilā l-jabali fa-ini staqarra makānahu fa-sawfa tarānī vs hinnēh māqôm ʾittî wᵉniṣṣabtā ʿal-haṣṣûr. The ending is reversed: in Exod Moses is sheltered by God's hand and sees his back (wᵉrāʾîtā ʾet-ʾăḥōrāy); in Q he sees nothing, the mountain is crushed (jaʿalahu dakkan), Moses falls stunned (kharra mūsā ṣaʿiqan) and repents (tubtu ilayka). Moses singled out by God's direct speech while being denied a vision: kallamahu rabbuhu; iṣṭafaytuka ʿalā n-nāsi bi-risālātī wa-bi-kalāmī vs dibber YHWH ʾel-mōšeh pānîm ʾel-pānîm; kî-māṣāʾtā ḥēn bᵉʿênay wāʾēdāʿăkā bᵉšēm. Q has speech without 'face to face'.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses asks to see God, his glory or God himself [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); What happens after God refuses to be seen by Moses [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The prophet asks to see God's glory (weight 6.7); God answers the prophet's request to see him: 'You will not see me' (weight 6.7); God speaks to the prophet face to face, as a man speaks to his friend (weight 6.0). Pair score 32.8.

Only in Mourning, the tent outside the camp, and Moses sees God's back: God refuses to go among the people lest he consume them on the way; Joshua, the young attendant, never leaves the tent; God tells the prophet: I know you by name and you have found favor; The people strip off their ornaments in mourning or penitence; The people stand at their tent doors and bow as the prophet goes to meet God; A tent of meeting pitched outside the camp where all who seek God go; God's own Presence (face) will go with the people; God declares he will be gracious to whom he will be gracious; God called Moses and drew him near in confidential converse (najiyy); Moses travels with his young servant (fata); After the calf the people mourn or repent of what they did [divergence between the texts]; God hides the prophet in a cleft of the rock, covers him with his hand, and lets him see only his back; and 6 more.

Only in Forty nights, the request to see God and the tablets: When God manifests himself to the mountain it is crushed to dust; The prophet falls down unconscious at the theophany and repents on waking; The tablets contain an exhortation and an explanation of all things; The appointed time on the mountain is thirty nights completed with ten more, making forty; Aaron and Hur left in charge while Moses is on the mountain; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Moses leaves a deputy (Aaron, with or without Hur) with the people while he is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; Moses' set period on the mountain is forty (days and nights, or nights) [divergence between the texts]; A mountain is shattered when God passes by or manifests himself [divergence between the texts]; Seeing God or breaking through to him brings death; A prophet spends forty days and forty nights in a set period; God seals (tab') the hearts of deniers so they do not hear; and 2 more.

title: New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue ↔ Ha-Mim: the Forgiver; the throne-bearers pray for the believers

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. mah-zzeh bəyādekā wayyōʾmer maṭṭeh, a one-word answer; wa-mā tilka bi-yamīnika yā Mūsā, qāla hiya ʿaṣāya atawakkaʾu ʿalayhā wa-ahushshu bihā ʿalā ghanamī wa-liya fīhā maʾāribu ukhrā. Same question; Q expands Moses' answer into a shepherd's self-portrait. hašlîkēhû ʾarṣâ ... wayhî lənāḥāš wayyānos mōšeh mippānāyw ... šəlaḥ yādəkā weʾĕḥōz bizənābô; alqihā ... fa-idhā hiya ḥayyatun tasʿā, qāla khudhhā wa-lā takhaf sa-nuʿīduhā sīratahā l-ūlā: thrown down, it becomes a snake; he is told to take it and it turns back. Moses flees in Exod; in Q he is told 'do not fear'. Exod: wəhinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat kaššāleg, a leprous hand, given so that the people will believe (ləmaʿan yaʾămînû). Q: takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾ, white 'without harm', which denies the disease, and given li-nuriyaka min āyātinā l-kubrā, a sign for Moses himself. Exod: speech trouble is an objection to the call, lōʾ ʾîš dəbārîm ʾānōkî ... kî kəbad-peh ûkəbad lāšôn ʾānōkî ... šəlaḥ-nāʾ bəyad-tišlāḥ, and God rebukes him, mî śām peh lāʾādām. Q: it is a prayer, rabbi shraḥ lī ṣadrī ... wa-ḥlul ʿuqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī, granted at once, qad ūtīta suʾlaka yā Mūsā. Who initiates, and the mood. Exod: God imposes Aaron in anger, wayyiḥar-ʾap YHWH bəmōšeh ... hălōʾ ʾahărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wəhāyâ-hûʾ yihyeh-ləkā ləpeh wəʾattâ tihyeh-lô lēʾlōhîm. Q: Moses asks for him, wa-jʿal lī wazīran min ahlī Hārūna akhī ushdud bihi azrī wa-ashrikhu fī amrī, so that they may glorify God much (kay nusabbiḥaka kathīrā). No anger, and no 'as God'.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Asked what is in his hand, the prophet lists his staff's uses: leaning, beating down leaves for sheep, other needs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' (weight 5.6); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4). Pair score 48.6.

Only in Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood: Wife saves her husband from a divine attack with her son's circumcision blood, calling him 'bridegroom of blood'; Two brothers meet and kiss at the mountain of God; God attacks the hero at a night lodging and seeks to kill him; God claims to make the mouth, the mute, the deaf, the seeing and the blind; The people believe the prophet's signs and bow in worship; Hero may return home because those seeking his life are dead; Wife cuts off her son's foreskin with a flint and touches it to the threatened man; The hero carries 'the staff of God' with which he performs signs; What Moses demands of Pharaoh in God's name [divergence between the texts]; God taught humankind by the pen (qalam) what it did not know; Moses' difficulty of speech, pleaded by himself or thrown at him [divergence between the texts]; How a people responds to a sign given to prove the messenger [contrast between the texts]; and 11 more.

Only in Moses at the fire in the holy valley Tuwa: The Hour is coming; God almost keeps it hidden so each soul is repaid for its striving; Prophet prays for his chest to be expanded and the knot of his tongue untied; Asked what is in his hand, the prophet lists his staff's uses: leaning, beating down leaves for sheep, other needs; The prophet asks that his brother be made his helper (wazīr) and partner in his mission; The call comes in the holy valley named Ṭuwā; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there [divergence between the texts]; The call comes in the holy valley named Ṭuwā [divergence between the texts]; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; Hero told to remove his sandals because the place is holy ground; A shepherd tending flocks comes to the mountain of God and is called; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed; The called one asks for a sign that it is God who speaks.

title: Signs for Moses, Aaron as mouthpiece, return to Egypt, the bridegroom of blood ↔ Moses and Aaron, Noah, Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass and the rained-upon town
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: aaron's role beside moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts].

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. wa-yaḍīqu ṣadrī wa-lā yanṭaliqu lisānī fa-arsil ilā Hārūna ~ kî khəvad peh û-khəvad lāšôn ʾānōkhî ... šəlaḥ nāʾ bə-yad tišlāḥ: Moses' tongue (lisān / lāšôn) is not free, and he asks God to send someone else. In the Quran he names Aaron himself. God's answer to Moses' reluctance: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm (anger; Aaron as mouth, Moses as God to him) ~ qāla kallā fa-dhhabā bi-āyātinā innā maʿakum mustamiʿūna: no anger and no 'as God'; both are sent as equals (fa-dhhabā, dual). evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. As at Q 27:10: wa-yyānās Mōše mip-pānāyw ~ wallā mudbiran wa-lam yuʿaqqib; Exodus' command to seize the snake's tail (wə-ʾĕḥōz bi-znāvô) becomes yā Mūsā aqbil wa-lā takhaf innaka mina l-āminīn, 'come forward and do not fear, you are safe'. Two signs, not three, and no leprosy: Exodus gives staff, leprous hand (məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg), and a third sign held in reserve, Nile water turned to blood (wə-hāyû lə-dām bay-yabbāšet), meant for doubting Israelites; the Quran has fa-dhānika burhānāni min rabbika ilā Firʿawna wa-malaʾihi, two proofs aimed at Pharaoh, the hand white 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ), and adds 'draw your arm to your side against fear'. Aaron's eloquence: in Exodus Moses says he is heavy of mouth, and God, angry, proposes Aaron himself: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... yādaʿtî kî dabbēr yədabbēr hûʾ ... wə-śamtā ʾet had-dəvārîm bə-fîw. In the Quran Moses proposes him, wa-akhī Hārūnu huwa afṣaḥu minnī lisānan fa-arsilhu maʿiya ridʾan yuṣaddiqunī, and God agrees without anger: sa-nashuddu ʿaḍudaka bi-akhīka. Aaron is a supporting witness (ridʾ, yuṣaddiqunī), not a mouth for Moses as God. rabbi innī qataltu minhum nafsan fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni ~ kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā: the old killing as an obstacle to going back. In Exodus God removes it unasked, in the Quran Moses raises it at the call.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses flees from his staff turned serpent, and God's response [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Moses' fear of being killed, on returning, for the Egyptian's death [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Moses' hand turned white as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); Prophet's hand turns leprous, white as snow, and is restored as a sign (weight 5.6); Prophet protests he is heavy of mouth and tongue or 'uncircumcised of lips' (weight 5.6); An eloquent brother is appointed to speak for the hero, who is 'as God' to him (weight 5.6); A staff thrown down becomes a serpent and turns back into a staff (weight 5.4). Pair score 46.8.

Only in The fire on the side of the Mount; the call from the tree; Aaron as helper: Moses says his brother Aaron is more eloquent of tongue and asks for him as a helper to confirm him; Moses is called from the tree on the right bank of the valley, in the blessed spot; God calls Moses from the fire, from a bush or a tree [divergence between the texts]; Prophet lodges in 'the cave' on Horeb, the mountain of God; Where and how Moses comes to the place of his call [divergence between the texts]; The thrown staff quivers like a jānn (small snake) and Moses turns and flees without looking back; Traveling with his family, the prophet sees a fire and goes to bring back a brand or find guidance there; A shepherd tending flocks comes to the mountain of God and is called; God appears in a bush that burns without being consumed.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. The magicians' end. Exod: they fail at the lice and say ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hiwʾ, but stay at court (they are struck by boils at 9:11), and Pharaoh's heart is hardened. Q: wa-ulqiya l-saḥaratu sājidīna qālū āmannā bi-rabbi l-ʿālamīna rabbi Mūsā wa-Hārūna. They convert at the first contest, are threatened with mutilation and crucifixion (la-uqaṭṭiʿanna aydiyakum wa-arjulakum min khilāfin thumma la-uṣallibannakum), and pray to die as muslims (wa-tawaffanā muslimīna). Grudging recognition becomes conversion and martyrdom. Exod: haʿtîrû ʾel-YHWH wə-yāsēr haṣ-ṣəfardəʿîm ... wa-ʾăšalləḥāh ʾet-hā-ʿām, then wa-yyarʾ Parʿōh kî hāyətāh hā-rəwāḥāh wə-hakhbēd ʾet-libbô. Q: yā Mūsā dʿu lanā rabbaka ... la-in kashafta ʿannā l-rijza la-nuʾminanna laka wa-la-nursilanna maʿaka banī Isrāʾīla ... idhā hum yankuthūna. The vow made under a plague and broken afterwards. Q adds a promise of faith (la-nuʾminanna) and says 'they break their word', where Exod says the heart was made heavy.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' (weight 6.7); Magicians fail to imitate a wonder and confess 'This is the finger of God' [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The dust of the earth becomes lice on man and beast (weight 6.3); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 6.0); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 5.8); King asks the prophet to intercede with God to remove a plague (weight 5.6); Prophet delivers God's demand 'Let my people go that they may serve me' (weight 5.4); Prophet's wonders are imitated by the king's magicians in a contest (weight 5.1); The king's heart is hardened (by himself or by God) so he refuses to release the people (weight 4.6). Pair score 52.2.

Only in Plagues 1-3: blood, frogs, lice: The dead frogs are piled in heaps and the land stinks; Egyptians dig around the Nile for drinkable water; Prophet lets the king choose when the plague should end, to prove God's power; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; How the defeated court magicians respond [divergence between the texts]; The king breaks his promise to release the people once a plague is lifted [divergence between the texts]; Prophet confronts the king at the river in the morning; Why Pharaoh and Egypt refuse despite the signs [divergence between the texts].

Only in Moses before Pharaoh, the magicians and the plagues: Pharaoh's people are struck with years of drought and lack of fruits before the plagues; Enemies attribute their misfortune to the prophet as a bad omen (tatayyur); their omen is with God; The magicians' spell bewitches the people's eyes and terrifies them; The magicians offer the prophet to throw first; he tells them to throw; Pharaoh is said to have his own gods, whom Moses would make him abandon; One of the Egyptian plagues is a flood (tufan); The tyrant threatens to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides and crucify the converts; The king's courtiers advise him how to deal with the prophet and his people [contrast between the texts]; Rulers fear that a people will leave the land, or drive them out of it [divergence between the texts]; The court magicians ask the king for a reward if they win and are promised closeness; Threatened believers say 'to our Lord we return' and pray for patience and to die as muslims; Pharaoh executes or threatens offenders by hanging, impaling or crucifixion; and 16 more.

title: Moses as god to Pharaoh; Aaron's staff becomes a tannin and swallows the magicians' staffs ↔ Moses, the houses as qibla, and Pharaoh's drowning faith

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Exod: Aaron's staff (wayyašlēk ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wayhî lətannîn), and the magicians really do the same, wayyaʿăśû gam-hēm ḥarṭummê miṣrayim bəlahăṭêhem kēn ... wayyihyû lətannînim, before wayyiblaʿ maṭṭēh-ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭōtām. Q: Moses' staff (alqi mā fī yamīnika talqaf mā ṣanaʿū), and the magicians' ropes and staffs only seem to move, yukhayyalu ilayhi min siḥrihim annahā tasʿā. The actor and the reality of the rival magic both change. Exod: God hardens, waʾănî ʾaqšeh ʾet-lēb parʿōh wəhirbêtî ʾet-ʾōtōtay, and wayyeḥĕzaq lēb parʿōh ... kaʾăšer dibber YHWH. Q: Pharaoh himself refuses, wa-la-qad araynāhu āyātinā kullahā fa-kadhdhaba wa-abā, and God's hand in it is not stated.

Exod 7:11 wa-yyiqrāʾ gam Parʿōh la-ḥăkhāmîm wə-la-mkhaššəfîm, Pharaoh simply summons them and they repeat the sign with their secret arts (bə-lahăṭêhem). Only in Jerusalem the exposed foundling, God's bride and the faithless harlot: An assembly stones the adulteress and hacks her with swords and burns her houses before many women; God gathers the adulteress's lovers, strips her naked before them and hands her over to be judged; The adorned bride trusts in her beauty and plays the harlot with every passer-by; Bride given a gold nose-ring and bracelets; King makes his son 'pass through the fire' after the abominations of the nations; Sons and daughters born to God are slaughtered and offered to idols as food; A newborn girl is cast into the open field unwashed, unsalted and unswaddled, with her navel cord uncut, loathed on the day of her birth; God spreads his garment-wing over the grown foundling, swears a covenant and takes the city as his wife, bathing, anointing, clothing and adorning her; Unlike other harlots, the city pays fees to her lovers instead of receiving them; Worship of other gods described as 'whoring after' them; God passes by the infant wallowing in her blood and says twice 'In your blood, live!'; Jerusalem's origin is Canaanite: 'your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite'; The unfaithful wife makes male images (tsalmei zakhar) from the gold and silver God gave her and fornicates with them; Political alliances with Egypt, Assyria and Chaldea pictured as harlotry with lovers ('big of flesh'); Man asked to spread his garment-wing over a woman as a sign of marriage.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. Q: wa-lā taksibu kullu nafsin illā ʿalayhā wa-lā taziru wāziratun wizra ukhrā. Ezek: han-nefeš ha-ḥōṭēʾt hîʾ tāmût bēn lōʾ-yiśśāʾ ba-ʿăwōn hā-ʾāv. Both use a verb of carrying (wazara / nāśāʾ) for guilt.

Shared motifs, rarest first: 'The soul that sins, it shall die': the son does not bear the father's iniquity nor the father the son's (weight 6.3); Fathers not put to death for children nor children for fathers (weight 5.8). Pair score 12.1.

Only in Sour grapes - individual responsibility and repentance: Exhortation: cast away your transgressions and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; why will you die?; Test case of three generations: righteous father, violent son, and a grandson who sees his father's sins and does not imitate them; Whether one person can carry another's sin [divergence between the texts]; No one may excuse himself on judgment day because his ancestors associated partners; If the wicked turns from his sins, none of his transgressions will be remembered; if the righteous turns away, his righteousness is forgotten; Catalogue of the righteous man: no eating on the mountains, no idols, no adultery, no menstrual intercourse, no oppression, returns pledges, feeds the hungry, clothes the naked, no interest; Proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes and the children's teeth are set on edge', abolished by God; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; People complain 'the way of the Lord is not fair'; God answers that it is their ways that are unfair; God does not desire the death of the wicked but that he turn from his way and live; A cloak taken in pledge must be returned before sunset; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; and 3 more.

Only in Tenfold reward; my life and death for God; no bearer bears another's burden: On the day some of the signs come, faith not believed before will not avail; My prayer, my rites, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds; God made you successors (khalāʾif) on the earth and raised some above others in rank to test you; The Prophet is commanded to be the first of those who submit (awwal al-muslimīn); God multiplies a good deed (tenfold) while an evil deed is requited only by its like; Whether guilt passes from parents to their descendants [contrast between the texts]; Those who split their religion into sects, each party exulting in what it has; Follow the religion (milla) of Abraham the ḥanīf, who was no idolater; Each person dies for his own sin.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Oath cluster: by the Mount (al-Tur), a book inscribed on unrolled parchment (raqq manshur), the frequented House, the raised roof and the swelling/kindled sea (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. hătiḥyênâ hāʿăṣāmôt hāʾēlleh ... yābəšû ʿaṣmôtênû wəʾābədâ tiqwātēnû; a-idhā kunnā ʿiẓāman wa-rufātan a-innā la-mabʿūthūna khalqan jadīdā: can dry bones (ʿăṣāmôt / ʿiẓām, cognate) live again? Ezek's doubters are the exiles in despair, and the bones are a figure for national restoration. Q's doubters are deniers mocking, and the answer is literal: alladhī faṭarakum awwala marra.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Deniers ask 'When we are bones and fragments, shall we be raised as a new creation?' (weight 5.4). Pair score 5.4.

Only in The valley of dry bones: God will open his people's graves, bring them up from their graves and bring them to the land of Israel; The exiles say 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off'; The prophet summons the breath (ruah) from the four winds to breathe into the slain so they live; The prophet is set down in a valley full of very many, very dry bones and led around among them; In the womb God makes the lump into bones and clothes the bones with flesh, then makes it another creation; God asks 'Can these bones live?' and the prophet answers 'Lord God, you know'; The revived dead stand on their feet, an exceedingly great army; God will put his own spirit within them and cause them to walk in his statutes; A multitude of dead revived [divergence between the texts]; The question whether God can make the dead live [divergence between the texts]; The question whether dead bones can live again, and who asks it [divergence between the texts]; A single cry or rebuke (zajra) and the dead stand looking; and 3 more.

Only in Gog's fall, seven years of burning weapons, the Valley of Hamon-Gog and the great feast of the birds: God strikes the bow from the invader's left hand and makes the arrows drop from his right hand; The nations will know that Israel went into exile for its own iniquity because God hid his face, not because he was weak; The carrion-eaters are sated at God's table with horses, charioteers, warriors and all men of war; God sends fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands; God will no longer hide his face from Israel, for he has poured out his spirit on the house of Israel; Israel plunders those who plundered them and despoils those who despoiled them; God invites every bird and beast to his great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel to eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of princes, as of rams, lambs, goats and Bashan bulls, till drunk with blood; All Israel buries the dead for seven months to purify the land; appointed men search the land and mark every human bone with a sign (tsiyyun) for the buriers; Gog and his horde are buried in the Valley of the Travelers east of the sea, renamed Valley of Hamon-Gog; a city is named Hamonah; Israel's townsfolk burn the enemy weapons (shields, bows, arrows, clubs, spears) as fuel for seven years, cutting no wood from the forest; Strong bulls of Bashan encircle the sufferer; Slain enemies become a portion for jackals or food for beasts and birds; and 6 more.

Gen: the rāqîaʿ divides waters from waters, wîhî mabdîl bên mayim lāmāyim. Q: heaven and earth themselves were one closed mass, kānatā ratqan fa-fataqnāhumā. What is divided differs: the waters in Gen, heaven from earth in Q. yišrəṣû hammayim šereṣ nepeš ḥayyâ ... wəʾēt kol-nepeš haḥayyâ hārōmeśet ʾăšer šārəṣû hammayim; wa-jaʿalnā mina l-māʾi kulla shayʾin ḥayy: life comes from water (nepeš ḥayyâ / shayʾin ḥayy). title: Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest ↔ Ha-Mim Fussilat: the veil between; creation in days; heaven as smoke
summary: These two units share 2 motifs: the order of creating heaven and earth and the days allotted to each [divergence between the texts], creation is completed in six days.

passages.note: The order of creating heaven and earth and the days allotted to each [divergence between the texts] (The order and the counting of the days. Gen: the firmament called šāmāyim on day 2 (yôm šēnî), dry land and plants on day 3, luminaries in the firmament on day 4, so heaven before dry earth, one work per day. Q: khalaqa l-arḍa fī yawmayni ... wa-qaddara fīhā aqwātahā fī arbaʿati ayyām ... thumma stawā ilā s-samāʾi wa-hiya dukhān ... fa-qaḍāhunna sabʿa samāwātin fī yawmayn. The earth is created first, its provisions in four days, and only then the seven heavens; the sums (2+4+2) are reckoned by the exegetes to six. There is no evening-and-morning formula, no seventh day, and the luminaries are 'lamps' of the lowest heaven.)

title: Creation in six days and the seventh-day rest ↔ Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood
summary: These two units share 1 motifs: god made the great lights: the sun to rule the day, the moon and stars to rule the night.

title: Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac ↔ Abraham's guests, the roasted calf and the laughing wife

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Who comes: wa-la-qad jāʾat rusulunā ibrāhīma bi-l-bushrā vs wayyērāʾ ʾēlāyw YHWH ... wᵉhinnēh šᵉlōšāh ʾănāšîm. Gen has YHWH himself appear in the form of three men; Q has 'our messengers', with no number and no appearance of God. Abraham at once brings a calf: fa-mā labitha an jāʾa bi-ʿijlin ḥanīdh (roasted) vs ʾel-habbāqār rāṣ ʾabrāhām wayyiqqaḥ ben-bāqār rak wāṭôb ... wayᵉmahēr (both stress haste). Q has no foot-washing, cakes, curds or milk. Reversed: in Gen the guests eat (wayyittēn lipnêhem wᵉhûʾ-ʿōmēd ʿălêhem taḥat hāʿēṣ wayyōʾkēlû); in Q their hands do not reach the food (fa-lammā raʾā aydiyahum lā taṣilu ilayhi nakirahum). cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14, b. Bava Metzia 86b (angels only seem to eat), outside the canon. Who is afraid and why: in Q Abraham is afraid because the guests will not eat (wa-awjasa minhum khīfatan qālū lā takhaf); in Gen it is Sarah who is afraid when caught laughing (wattᵉkaḥēš śārāh lēʾmōr lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾāh). The order and the answer change: in Gen Sarah overhears the promise at the tent door and then laughs inwardly (wattiṣḥaq śārāh bᵉqirbāh), and God rebukes her (lāmmāh zeh ṣāḥăqāh śārāh), she denies it (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî); in Q she is standing by and laughs first (wa-mraʾatuhu qāʾimatun fa-ḍaḥikat), then receives the tidings, with no rebuke and no denial. ṣḥq / ḍḥk are cognate. The promise of a son: fa-basharnāhā bi-isḥāqa wa-min warāʾi isḥāqa yaʿqūb vs šôb ʾāšûb ʾēlêkā kāʿēt ḥayyāh wᵉhinnēh-bēn lᵉśārāh ʾištekā. It is said to Sarah directly in Q, to Abraham in Gen (Sarah only overhears); Q names Isaac and adds Jacob after him; Gen names no child here and adds a date (lammôʿēd ... kāʿēt ḥayyāh).
Passages are shown for the 10 rarest of 12 shared motifs; the full list follows.

Shared motifs, rarest first: When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who is afraid during the visit of the heavenly guests, and why [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Who Abraham's visitors are (weight 6.7); Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal he serves [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age (weight 6.7); A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests (weight 6.3); The old wife overhears the promise of a son at the tent door and laughs (weight 6.3); A divine messenger announces a son to a barren couple [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.0); 'Is anything too wondrous for the LORD?' (weight 6.0); God appears as three men who visit the patriarch (weight 5.8); Patriarch or matriarch laughs at the promise of a child in old age (weight 5.6); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them (weight 5.1). Pair score 74.5.

Only in Three visitors at Mamre and the promise of Isaac: Child promised to a woman past childbearing age; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Heavenly visitors eat a human meal; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age [divergence between the texts]; The aged father asks how he can have a son when his wife is barren and he is very old [divergence between the texts]; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; Who Abraham's visitors are [divergence between the texts]; The patriarch tells his unknown guests 'we are afraid of you' [divergence between the texts]; Patriarch or matriarch laughs at the promise of a child in old age [divergence between the texts]; Sarah's reaction to the announcement of a son [divergence between the texts]; Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal [divergence between the texts]; Sacred oak or terebinth marks a sanctuary site (Moreh, Mamre); and 1 more.

Only in Abraham's guests, the roasted calf and the laughing wife: Abraham is forbearing, sighing (awwah) and penitent; Abraham's angelic guests do not stretch their hands to the food, and he is afraid; The annunciation names Isaac 'and after Isaac, Jacob'; Promised son born to aged parents at the appointed time; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response; How God answers Abraham's plea for the people of Sodom [divergence between the texts]; When and why Sarah laughs, and how it is answered; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10).

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): echo. wə-hinnēh-ḇēn lə-śārâ ʾišteḵā vs. wa-basharnāhu bi-Isḥāqa nabiyyan mina ṣ-ṣāliḥīn. The announcement of Isaac's birth. In Gen it comes four chapters before the Aqedah; in Q it comes after the sacrifice, as a further reward, and calls Isaac a prophet.
Shared motifs, rarest first: A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name (weight 5.2). Pair score 5.2.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Who the visitors are. Genesis: wa-yērāʾ ʾēlâw YHWH bə-ʾēlōnê mamrēʾ ... wə-hinnēh šəlōšâ ʾănāšîm (YHWH appears, as three men; YHWH himself speaks in 18:13). Quran: ḍayfu ibrāhīma l-mukramīn, addressed as ayyuhā l-mursalūn (51:31): honored guests who are 'sent ones', no number, and God is not among them. The welcome. Genesis: Abraham runs to meet them (wa-yyāroṣ liqrāʾṯām), bows to the ground and begs ʾăḏōnāy ʾim nāʾ māṣāʾṯî ḥēn bə-ʿênêḵā, then wa-yəmahēr ʾaḇrāhām hā-ʾōhĕlâ ʾel śārâ. Quran: the guests speak first, fa-qālū salāman qāla salāmun qawmun munkarūn (Abraham returns the greeting and finds them strange), then fa-rāgha ilā ahlihi (he slipped off to his household). Same hurried move to the tent; the bow and the plea are absent, and Abraham's unease (munkarūn) is added. wa-yiqqaḥ ben bāqār raḵ wā-ṭôḇ ... wa-yiqqaḥ ḥemʾâ wə-ḥālāḇ û-ḇen hab-bāqār ... wa-yittēn lip̄nêhem vs. fa-jāʾa bi-ʿijlin samīnin fa-qarrabahu ilayhim. Genesis: a tender, good calf with curds and milk; Quran: a fat calf only. Reversal: in Genesis the visitors eat: wə-hûʾ ʿōmēḏ ʿălêhem taḥaṯ hā-ʿēṣ wa-yyōʾḵēlû. In the Quran they do not: qāla a-lā taʾkulūn, fa-awjasa minhum khīfatan, qālū lā takhaf. The refusal to eat reveals that they are angels and frightens Abraham. cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14 and b. Bava Metzia 86b (the angels only seemed to eat), a solution to the same problem; not in the HB. wə-hinnēh ḇēn lə-śārâ ʾištekā; lam-môʿēḏ ʾāšûḇ ʾēleḵā kā-ʿēṯ ḥayyâ û-lə-śārâ ḇēn vs. wa-bashsharūhu bi-ghulāmin ʿalīm. Genesis promises a son to Sarah with a set time; the Quran gives the good news to Abraham of 'a knowing boy', with no time and no name. Sarah's reaction, changed from inner laughter to an open cry. Genesis: wat-tiṣḥaq śārâ bə-qirbāh lēʾmōr ʾaḥărê ḇəlōṯî ... wa-ʾḏōnî zāqēn; God asks lāmmâ zeh ṣāḥăqâ śārâ and she denies it out of fear (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾâ). Quran: fa-aqbalati mraʾatuhu fī ṣarratin fa-ṣakkat wajhahā wa-qālat ʿajūzun ʿaqīm (she came forward crying out, struck her face and said 'a barren old woman!'). The messengers answer ka-dhālika qāla rabbuki innahu huwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm: no rebuke, no denial, no laughter (ṣ-ḥ-q, the pun on Isaac's name, is gone).

passages.text: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֶּ֣ה נָּא אֲדֹנַ֗י ס֣וּרוּ נָ֠א אֶל בֵּ֨ית עַבְדְּכֶ֤ם וְלִ֨ינוּ֙ וְרַחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּ֖ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֣ם לְדַרְכְּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י בָרְח֖וֹב נָלִֽין

passages.note: How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts] (Lot's response to the guests is reversed: in Gen he rises to meet them, bows and presses them to stay (wayyāqom liqrāʾtām wayyištaḥû ... wayyipṣar-bām mᵉʾōd ... wayyaʿaś lāhem mišteh); in Q he is distressed and helpless on their account (sīʾa bihim wa-ḍāqa bihim dharʿan wa-qāla hādhā yawmun ʿaṣīb).)
passages.text: وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالَ هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ

passages.note: When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts] (When they leave and when the blow falls: Q, by night, the destruction appointed for morning (bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layli ... inna mawʿidahumu ṣ-ṣubḥu a-laysa ṣ-ṣubḥu bi-qarīb); Gen, the angels hurry him at dawn (kᵉmô haššaḥar ʿālāh wayyāʾîṣû) and the fire falls once the sun has risen and Lot is in Zoar (haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wᵉlôṭ bāʾ ṣōʿărāh).)
passages.text: וּכְמוֹ֙ הַשַּׁ֣חַר עָלָ֔ה וַיָּאִ֥יצוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים בְּל֣וֹט לֵאמֹ֑ר קוּם֩ קַ֨ח אֶֽת אִשְׁתְּךָ֜ וְאֶת שְׁתֵּ֤י בְנֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ הַנִּמְצָאֹ֔ת פֶּן תִּסָּפֶ֖ה בַּעֲוֺ֥ן הָעִֽיר

passages.note: When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts] (When they leave and when the blow falls: Q, by night, the destruction appointed for morning (bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layli ... inna mawʿidahumu ṣ-ṣubḥu a-laysa ṣ-ṣubḥu bi-qarīb); Gen, the angels hurry him at dawn (kᵉmô haššaḥar ʿālāh wayyāʾîṣû) and the fire falls once the sun has risen and Lot is in Zoar (haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wᵉlôṭ bāʾ ṣōʿărāh).)
passages.text: הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ יָצָ֣א עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ וְל֖וֹט בָּ֥א צֹֽעֲרָה

passages.text: قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ

passages.note: Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city (Lot is told to take his family out: fa-asri bi-ahlika vs qûm qaḥ ʾet-ʾištᵉkā wᵉʾet-šᵉtê bᵉnōtêkā ... pen-tissāpeh baʿăwōn hāʿîr. Gen adds the sons-in-law who think he is joking (wayᵉhî kimṣaḥēq bᵉʿênê ḥătānāyw).)
passages.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים אֶל ל֗וֹט עֹ֚ד מִֽי לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה חָתָן֙ וּבָנֶ֣יךָ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר לְךָ֖ בָּעִ֑יר הוֹצֵ֖א מִן הַמָּקֽוֹם

passages.note: What Lot says to the townsmen (Lot offers his daughters: hāʾulāʾi banātī hunna aṭharu lakum fa-ttaqū llāha wa-lā tukhzūni fī ḍayfī a-laysa minkum rajulun rashīd vs ʾal-nāʾ ʾaḥay tārēʿû hinnēh-nāʾ lî šᵉtê bānôt ... wᵉʿăśû lāhen kaṭṭôb bᵉʿênêkem raq lāʾănāšîm hāʾēl ʾal-taʿăśû dābār. The terms differ: in Gen 'do to them as you please'; in Q 'they are purer for you', with an appeal to fear God and to right-minded men. Exegesis reads Q as lawful marriage.)
passages.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אַל נָ֥א אַחַ֖י תָּרֵֽעוּ

passages.text: הִנֵּה נָ֨א לִ֜י שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יָדְעוּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ אוֹצִֽיאָה נָּ֤א אֶתְהֶן֙ אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ן כַּטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם רַ֠ק לָֽאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵל֙ אַל תַּעֲשׂ֣וּ דָבָ֔ר כִּֽי עַל כֵּ֥ן בָּ֖אוּ בְּצֵ֥ל קֹרָתִֽי

The terms differ: in Gen 'do to them as you please'; in Q 'they are purer for you', with an appeal to fear God and to right-minded men. Exegesis reads Q as lawful marriage.)
passages.text: وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِى هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِى ضَيْفِىٓ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَّشِيدٌ

passages.note: Lot's townspeople turn on him (The townsmen besiege Lot's house: wa-jāʾahu qawmuhu yuhraʿūna ilayhi vs nāsabbû ʿal-habbayit minnaʿar wᵉʿad-zāqēn ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wᵉnēdʿāh ʾōtām. Their answer differs: in Gen they turn on Lot as an alien who plays the judge (hāʾeḥād bāʾ-lāgûr wayyišpōṭ šāpôṭ) and try to break the door; in Q they only say la-qad ʿalimta mā lanā fī banātika min ḥaqqin wa-innaka la-taʿlamu mā nurīd.)
passages.text: טֶרֶם֮ יִשְׁכָּבוּ֒ וְאַנְשֵׁ֨י הָעִ֜יר אַנְשֵׁ֤י סְדֹם֙ נָסַ֣בּוּ עַל הַבַּ֔יִת מִנַּ֖עַר וְעַד זָקֵ֑ן כָּל הָעָ֖ם מִקָּצֶֽה

passages.note: The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts] (The guests disclose their errand: yā lūṭu innā rusulu rabbika lan yaṣilū ilayka vs kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh ... wayᵉšallᵉḥēnû YHWH lᵉšaḥătāh. In Gen the angels first pull Lot inside and strike the mob with blindness (hikkû bassanwērîm); in Q, where Lot wishes for strength or a strong support (law anna lī bikum quwwatan aw āwī ilā ruknin shadīd), only their word assures him.)
