evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/03-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Lot's response to the guests is reversed: in Gen he rises to meet them, bows and presses them to stay (wayyāqom liqrāʾtām wayyištaḥû ... wayyipṣar-bām mᵉʾōd ... wayyaʿaś lāhem mišteh); in Q he is distressed and helpless on their account (sīʾa bihim wa-ḍāqa bihim dharʿan wa-qāla hādhā yawmun ʿaṣīb). The townsmen besiege Lot's house: wa-jāʾahu qawmuhu yuhraʿūna ilayhi vs nāsabbû ʿal-habbayit minnaʿar wᵉʿad-zāqēn ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wᵉnēdʿāh ʾōtām. Their answer differs: in Gen they turn on Lot as an alien who plays the judge (hāʾeḥād bāʾ-lāgûr wayyišpōṭ šāpôṭ) and try to break the door; in Q they only say la-qad ʿalimta mā lanā fī banātika min ḥaqqin wa-innaka la-taʿlamu mā nurīd. Lot offers his daughters: hāʾulāʾi banātī hunna aṭharu lakum fa-ttaqū llāha wa-lā tukhzūni fī ḍayfī a-laysa minkum rajulun rashīd vs ʾal-nāʾ ʾaḥay tārēʿû hinnēh-nāʾ lî šᵉtê bānôt ... wᵉʿăśû lāhen kaṭṭôb bᵉʿênêkem raq lāʾănāšîm hāʾēl ʾal-taʿăśû dābār. The terms differ: in Gen 'do to them as you please'; in Q 'they are purer for you', with an appeal to fear God and to right-minded men. Exegesis reads Q as lawful marriage. The guests disclose their errand: yā lūṭu innā rusulu rabbika lan yaṣilū ilayka vs kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh ... wayᵉšallᵉḥēnû YHWH lᵉšaḥătāh. In Gen the angels first pull Lot inside and strike the mob with blindness (hikkû bassanwērîm); in Q, where Lot wishes for strength or a strong support (law anna lī bikum quwwatan aw āwī ilā ruknin shadīd), only their word assures him. Lot is told to take his family out: fa-asri bi-ahlika vs qûm qaḥ ʾet-ʾištᵉkā wᵉʾet-šᵉtê bᵉnōtêkā ... pen-tissāpeh baʿăwōn hāʿîr. Gen adds the sons-in-law who think he is joking (wayᵉhî kimṣaḥēq bᵉʿênê ḥătānāyw). When they leave and when the blow falls: Q, by night, the destruction appointed for morning (bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layli ... inna mawʿidahumu ṣ-ṣubḥu a-laysa ṣ-ṣubḥu bi-qarīb); Gen, the angels hurry him at dawn (kᵉmô haššaḥar ʿālāh wayyāʾîṣû) and the fire falls once the sun has risen and Lot is in Zoar (haššemeš yāṣāʾ ʿal-hāʾāreṣ wᵉlôṭ bāʾ ṣōʿărāh).

Pair score 86.5.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest; and 28 more.

Only in Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil: The angels tell Lot the destruction is appointed for the morning: 'is not the morning near?'; Lot wishes he had strength or a strong support to take refuge in; Lot's wife is among those who stay behind and perish; Stones of baked clay (sijjil), in layers, each marked by the Lord, rain on the town; A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited; God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than the sword.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. Gen: Lot rises to meet them at the gate, bows, presses them to stay and bakes maṣṣôt. Q: Lot greets them coldly, innakum qawmun munkarūn ('you are strangers'). Hospitality is replaced by unease, as with Abraham. Order reversed. Gen: first the mob (19:4-11), then the angels reveal kî-mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet-hammāqôm hazzeh (19:13). Q: the messengers state their mission and order the flight (15:63-66, dābira hāʾulāʾi maqṭūʿun muṣbiḥīn), and only then do the townsmen come (wa-jāʾa ahlu l-madīnati yastabshirūn). Gen: ʾal-nāʾ ʾaḥay tārēʿû hinnēh-nāʾ lî šətê bānôt ʾăšer lōʾ-yādəʿû ʾîš ... waʿăśû lāhen kaṭṭôb bəʿênêkem. Q: hāʾulāʾi ḍayfī fa-lā tafḍaḥūni wa-ttaqū llāha ... hāʾulāʾi banātī in kuntum fāʿilīn. Q keeps the offer but drops 'do with them as you please' and adds an appeal to fear God (Q's form is open to the later reading of marriage). hāʾeḥād bāʾ-lāgûr wayyišpōṭ šāpôṭ, the townsmen resent the sojourner judging them; a-wa-lam nanhaka ʿani l-ʿālamīn, they forbade him to take in outsiders. Both turn on Lot's status as an outsider to the town. Gen: at dawn (kəmô haššaḥar ʿālâ) the angels drag the lingering Lot out by the hand; ʾal-tabbîṭ ʾaḥărêkā. Q: by night, fa-asri bi-ahlika bi-qiṭʿin mina l-layl wa-ttabiʿ adbārahum wa-lā yaltafit minkum aḥad: no hesitation, and Lot walks behind his family. Gen: her fate follows from her act, wattabbēṭ ʾištô mēʾaḥărāyw wattəhî nəṣîb melaḥ. Q: her fate is decreed in advance, qaddarnā innahā la-mina l-ghābirīn. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. The sin: Genesis has one night's event, the townsmen demanding Lot's two guests, hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wə-nēdəʿâ ʾōtām; the Quran has a standing practice of the whole people, a-taʾtūna dh-dhukrāna mina l-ʿālamīna wa-tadharūna mā khalaqa lakum rabbukum min azwājikum. The Quran has no guests, angels or hospitality, and Lot preaches as 'their brother' and a trustworthy messenger (26:161-162), which Genesis' Lot never does. la-in lam tantahi yā Lūṭu la-takūnanna mina l-mukhrajīna ~ hāʾeḥād bāʾ lāgûr wa-yyišpōṭ šāfôṭ ʿattâ nāraʿ ləkhā mēhem: the people turn on Lot as an outsider who presumes to judge them; Genesis threatens worse harm than to the guests, the Quran threatens expulsion. Why Lot is saved: Gen 19:29 wa-yyizkōr ʾĕlōhîm ʾet ʾAvrāhām wa-yšallaḥ ʾet Lôṭ, for Abraham's sake, and the angels drag the hesitating family out (wa-yyitmahmāh, 19:16); Q 26:169-170 Lot prays rabbi najjinī wa-ahlī mimmā yaʿmalūna and God saves him and his family in answer, for his own sake. Lot neither hesitates nor depends on Abraham. illā ʿajūzan fī l-ghābirīna ~ wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ: the one family member lost. Genesis names her Lot's wife and says why (she looked back) and how (pillar of salt); the Quran says only 'an old woman among those who stayed behind', with no looking back and no salt. wa-amṭarnā ʿalayhim maṭaran fa-sāʾa maṭaru l-mundharīna ~ wa-YHWH himṭîr ʿal Sədōm ... gofrît wā-ʾēš: the same verb (amṭara / himṭîr); the Quran does not name sulphur and fire, and Sodom is never named.

Shared motifs, rarest first: What the sin of Lot's townsmen was [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Lot's people threaten to expel him (weight 6.3); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 5.8); Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.8); Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt (weight 5.6); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 44.6.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 34 more.

Only in Lot and his people: Lot's family is saved except an old woman among those who stayed behind; Lot condemns his people for approaching males and leaving the wives God created for them; The town that was rained on with an evil rain (Lot's) is passed by travelers; Formula: 'their brother' (akhūhum) Noah/Hud/Salih/Lot is a trustworthy messenger sent to his people; Refrain closing each episode: 'In that is a sign, yet most of them do not believe; your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful'.

Eager hospitality becomes dismay. innā muhlikū ahli hādhihi l-qaryati inna ahlahā kānū ẓālimīna ... innā munzilūna ʿalā ahli hādhihi l-qaryati rijzan mina s-samāʾi ~ kî mašḥitîm ʾănaḥnû ʾet ham-māqôm haz-zeh ... wa-yšallə ḥēnû YHWH ləšaḥătāh: the messengers declare they are sent to destroy 'this place / this town'. In Genesis they say it to Lot; in the Quran first to Abraham, then to Lot. illā mraʾataka kānat mina l-ghābirīna ~ wat-tabbēṭ ʾištô mē-ʾaḥărāyw wat-təhî nəṣîv melaḥ: the wife's fate is known in advance and told to Abraham and Lot in the Quran; Genesis tells it as her own act during the flight.

Shared motifs, rarest first: How Lot receives the divine messengers [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city (weight 6.7); Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom (weight 6.0); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 5.8); Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt (weight 5.6); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 40.7.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 35 more.

Only in Lot and the destruction of his town: The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them; Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi); Abraham's plea when told that the city of Lot will be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; The sin of Sodom was pride, surfeit of bread and careless ease, not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy; A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo. What falls on the city. Genesis: wa-YHWH himṭîr ʿal səḏōm wə-ʿal ʿămōrâ goprîṯ wā-ʾēš mē-ʾēṯ YHWH min haš-šāmāyim (sulfur and fire rained from YHWH). Quran: li-nursila ʿalayhim ḥijāratan min ṭīnin musawwamatan ʿinda rabbika li-l-musrifīn (stones of clay, each marked by your Lord for the transgressors). Fire and sulfur become marked clay stones (cf. Q 11:82 sijjīl). One household rescued. Genesis: ʿōḏ mî ləḵā p̄ōh ḥāṯān û-ḇānêḵā û-ḇənōṯêḵā ... hôṣēʾ min ham-māqôm; the angels seize Lot's hand and his wife's and daughters' (wa-yyaḥăzîqû hā-ʾănāšîm bə-yāḏô ...) because of YHWH's pity (bə-ḥemlaṯ YHWH ʿālâw), and Lot hesitates (wa-yyiṯmahmāh). Quran: fa-akhrajnā man kāna fīhā mina l-muʾminīna fa-mā wajadnā fīhā ghayra baytin mina l-muslimīn. Lot's household is defined by faith (muʾminūn, muslimūn), not kinship; the hesitation, the sons-in-law and the wife's fate (19:26) are not told here. wə-hinnēh ʿālâ qîṭōr hā-ʾāreṣ kə-qîṭōr hak-kiḇšān (Abraham sees the smoke over the plain) vs. wa-taraknā fīhā āyatan li-lladhīna yakhāfūna l-ʿadhāba l-alīm. The aftermath seen by Abraham becomes a lasting sign for later people.

Shared motifs, rarest first: God left in the destroyed city a sign for those who fear the painful punishment (weight 6.7); Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out (weight 6.7); What falls from heaven on Sodom [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them (weight 5.1); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 41.4.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest; and 35 more.

Only in Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah: On 'Ad God sent the barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim), which left everything like rotten bones; Abraham brings a fattened calf but the guests do not eat, and he becomes afraid of them; The honored guests enter saying 'Peace' and Abraham replies 'Peace, strangers (qawm munkarun)'; The guests announce to Abraham a knowing (or wise) son ('alim); Thamud were told 'Enjoy yourselves for a while', defied the command and were seized by the thunderbolt while they looked on; Abraham's wife comes forward crying out, strikes her face and says 'A barren old woman!'; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Heavenly visitors eat a human meal; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response [divergence between the texts]; Who Abraham's visitors are [divergence between the texts]; In Lot's town only one house of submitters (muslimin) was found, and the believers were brought out; and 13 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo, parallel. The mob blinded at Lot's door. Genesis: ʾayyēh hā-ʾănāšîm ... hôṣîʾēm ʾēlênû wə-nēḏəʿāh ʾōṯām; the angels (hā-ʾănāšîm) strike them bas-sanwērîm and they weary themselves finding the door. Quran: wa-la-qad rāwadūhu ʿan ḍayfihi fa-ṭamasnā aʿyunahum fa-dhūqū ʿadhābī wa-nudhur (God says 'We blotted out their eyes'). The striking passes from the angel-guests to God himself, and the search for the door is dropped. Rescue at daybreak: û-ḵəmô haš-šaḥar ʿālâ wa-yyāʾîṣû ham-malʾāḵîm bə-lôṭ vs. illā āla lūṭin najjaynāhum bi-saḥar (Hebrew šaḥar 'dawn', Arabic saḥar 'the hour before dawn'). Why Lot is saved. Genesis: wa-yyizkōr ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ ʾaḇrāhām wa-yšallaḥ ʾeṯ lôṭ mit-tôḵ ha-hăp̄ēḵâ (for Abraham's sake), and earlier bə-ḥemlaṯ YHWH ʿālâw (19:16, God's pity in spite of his delay). Quran: najjaynāhum bi-saḥarin niʿmatan min ʿindinā ka-dhālika najzī man shakar (a favor from us; so we reward whoever is grateful). Rescue for Abraham's merit becomes reward for Lot's own gratitude. goprîṯ wā-ʾēš mē-ʾēṯ YHWH min haš-šāmāyim vs. innā arsalnā ʿalayhim ḥāṣiban (a storm of stones). As in Q 51:33 the Quran's Sodom is stoned, not burned. Lot's warning disbelieved: qûmû ṣəʾû min ham-māqôm haz-zeh kî mašḥîṯ YHWH ʾeṯ hā-ʿîr wa-yhî ḵi-mṣaḥēq bə-ʿênê ḥăṯānâw vs. wa-la-qad andharahum baṭshatanā fa-tamāraw bi-n-nudhur. Genesis: only his sons-in-law, who take it as a joke; Quran: the whole people, who dispute the warnings.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Lot's family is saved at the time before dawn (bi-sahar) while a storm of stones (hasib) destroys the rest (weight 6.7); Who strikes the Sodom mob's eyes [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); What falls from heaven on Sodom [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The righteous man's warning is taken as a joke by his own relatives (weight 6.3); Attackers struck with blindness and cannot find the door (weight 6.3); Townsmen surround the house and demand the male guest for sexual abuse (weight 6.0); Hero's family saved with him [divergence between the texts] (weight 5.4); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 48.5.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 34 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml): parallel. wa-l-muʾtafikātu bi-l-khāṭiʾa ... fa-ʿaṣaw rasūla rabbihim fa-akhadhahum ~ wa-yyahăfōk ʾet he-ʿārîm hā-ʾēl: the cities named only as 'the overturned ones'. The Quran gives the reason as disobeying 'the messenger of their Lord'; Genesis gives no messenger to Sodom except the visiting angels.
Shared motifs, rarest first: Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: A small town is spared at the refugee's request (Zoar, 'small'); Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; Deniers pray: 'If this is the truth from you, rain stones on us from the sky'; God rains destruction on Lot's town [divergence between the texts]; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; The fate of Lot's wife [divergence between the texts]; God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 41 more.

Only in Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne: 'Ad were destroyed by a furious wind for seven nights and eight days, lying felled like hollow palm trunks; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears; That day eight (angels) bear the Throne of your Lord above them; At a single blast on the trumpet, the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing; Thamud were destroyed by the Overwhelming (al-tagiya, the Blast); Rhetorical opening: 'The Reality (al-haqqa)! What is the Reality? And what will make you know what the Reality is?'; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; Four living creatures (hayyot) of human form bear the divine throne [divergence between the texts]; The overturned city (al-mu'tafika, Sodom) God hurled down and covered with what covered it; A roaring cold wind (sarsar) on a day of continuous ill omen plucks men away like trunks of uprooted palms; The sky splits and is frail that day, and the angels are on its borders; When the Event (al-waqi'a) befalls, none can deny it: it abases and exalts; and 4 more.
Lot's guests and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Hebrew.
Al-Haqqa: Thamud and 'Ad, the running ship, the single trumpet blast, the sky split and eight bearing the Throne: tagged by Claude (model), reading the Arabic.

Gen 2:19 wa-yyābēʾ ʾel hā-ʾādām lirʾôt mah yyiqrāʾ lô ... wa-yyiqrāʾ hā-ʾādām šēmôt: God brings the animals 'to see what he would call them' and the man invents the names; Q 2:31 wa-ʿallama ādama l-asmāʾa kullahā thumma ʿaraḍahum ʿalā l-malāʾikati: God teaches Adam all the names and displays the creatures to the angels as a test, ending innī aʿlamu ghayba s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ (2:33). Human initiative before an observing God becomes knowledge given by an all-knowing God, and the scene becomes a contest with the angels. Gen 2:8 gan bĕ-ʿēden miqqedem, 2:16 mi-kkōl ʿēṣ ha-gān ʾākōl tōʾkēl (said to the man alone, before the woman is made); Q 2:35 uskun anta wa-zawjuka l-jannata wa-kulā minhā raghadan ḥaythu shiʾtumā: 'the Garden' with no place in the east, and the permission is given to both (dual) together. The tree has no name (no 'knowledge of good and evil'); the sanction is to become wrongdoers, not death.

title: Birth of Isaac and expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael ↔ Abraham, Ishmael and the House
summary: These two units share 2 motifs: whether ishmael is with abraham or sent away [contrast between the texts], abraham prays that the town be made secure and its people provided with fruits.

passages.note: Whether Ishmael is with Abraham or sent away [contrast between the texts] (Gen 21:14 wa-yyiqqaḥ leḥem wĕ-ḥēmat mayim ... wĕ-ʾet ha-yyeled wa-yšallĕḥehā: Abraham sends Ishmael away with his mother, and only God's promise follows him (21:13 gam ʾet ben hā-ʾāmâ lĕ-gôy ʾăśîmennû); Q 2:125-128 ʿahidnā ilā ibrāhīma wa-ismāʿīla an ṭahhirā baytiya ... rabbanā wa-jʿalnā muslimayni laka: Ishmael is with Abraham as co-builder and co-petitioner, under the same covenant charge (ʿahidnā). evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml): divergence. Placement of the 'test'. Gen opens with it, wə-hā-ʾĕlōhîm nissâ ʾeṯ-ʾaḇrāhām, so the reader knows from the start that it is a trial. Q names it only after the rescue: inna hādhā la-huwa l-balāʾu l-mubīn. Gen's closing reason, kî ʿattâ yāḏaʿtî kî-yərēʾ ʾĕlōhîm ʾattâ (now I know, 22:12), has no counterpart: in Q God does not come to know. How the command comes. Gen: direct divine speech, qaḥ-nāʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā ... wə-lek-ləḵā ʾel-ʾereṣ ha-mmōriyyâ wə-haʿălēhû šām lə-ʿōlâ (a burnt offering at a named place). Q: a dream reported by the father, innī arā fī l-manāmi annī adhbaḥuka (I see in sleep that I slaughter you), with no place, no mountain and no ʿōlâ. Q's dhabaḥa is cognate with Hebrew zāḇaḥ, while Gen uses ʿōlâ and liš-ḥōṭ (22:10). Who the son is. Gen names him three times over: ʾeṯ-binḵā ʾeṯ-yəḥîḏəḵā ʾăšer-ʾāhaḇtā ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq. Q has only bi-ghulāmin ḥalīm (a forbearing boy) and announces Isaac only after the episode, wa-basharnāhu bi-Isḥāqa nabiyyan mina ṣ-ṣāliḥīn (37:112). This leaves the victim unnamed, and many exegetes read him as Ishmael. The 'only' (yāḥîḏ) son of Gen is not said. Who speaks, and what the son knows. Gen: Isaac does not know. He asks hinnēh hā-ʾēš wə-hā-ʿēṣîm wə-ʾayyēh ha-śśeh lə-ʿōlâ, and Abraham gives the veiled answer ʾĕlōhîm yirʾeh-lô ha-śśeh ... bənî. Q: the father tells him openly and asks his view, fa-nẓur mādhā tarā, and the son consents, yā-abati fʿal mā tuʾmaru sa-tajidunī in shāʾa llāhu mina ṣ-ṣābirīn. The address pair ʾāḇî / bənî matches yā-abati / yā-bunayya. Isaac's silence becomes the son's active submission. The act. Gen: wood laid on Isaac, fire and knife, an altar built, wa-yyaʿăqōḏ ʾeṯ-yiṣḥāq bənô wa-yyāśem ʾōṯô ʿal-ha-mmizbēaḥ mi-mmaʿal lā-ʿēṣîm, knife raised. Q: fa-lammā aslamā wa-tallahu li-l-jabīn, both 'submitted' and he laid him on his brow. No binding (ʿăqēḏâ), no altar, no wood, no fire and no three-day journey. The decisive word is the dual aslamā (both of them submitted). Who stops it, and why. Gen: wa-yyiqrāʾ ʾēlâw malʾaḵ YHWH min-ha-ššāmayim ... ʾaḇrāhām ʾaḇrāhām wa-yyōʾmer hinnēnî; ʾal-tišlaḥ yāḏəḵā ʾel-ha-nnaʿar, because Abraham fears God. Q: wa-nādaynāhu an yā-Ibrāhīmu qad ṣaddaqta r-ruʾyā. God calls in the first person plural, with no angel and no hinnēnî. The reason is that Abraham has already fulfilled the dream, not a prohibition.

Only in The binding of Isaac (Aqedah): The son to be sacrificed is called the only, beloved son; Place of sacrifice named 'YHWH will see/provide' on the mount of the LORD; Son asks his father where the sacrificial lamb is; The son carries the wood for his own sacrifice; Three-day journey to the mountain of sacrifice; Descendants will possess the gate of their enemies; Called by name, the hero answers 'Here I am' (hineni); All families of the earth will be blessed through the patriarch; God swears by himself; Descendants promised to be as countless as the dust, stars or sand.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo. Q 2:35 wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi sh-shajarata 'do not come near this tree' is God's own wording; in Genesis the extension is the woman's addition: Gen 3:3 lōʾ tōʾkĕlû mimmennû wĕ-lōʾ tiggĕʿû bô 'nor touch it', which God had not said (2:17). Gen 3:1, 3:13 ha-nnāḥāš hāyâ ʿārûm ... ha-nnāḥāš hiššîʾanî: a cunning serpent deceives the woman, who eats first and gives to the man (3:6); Q 2:36 fa-azallahumā sh-shayṭānu ʿanhā: Satan makes both slip (dual). No serpent, no woman eating first, no woman as channel of the sin. Gen 3:23-24 wa-yšallĕḥēhû YHWH ʾĕlōhîm ... wa-ygāreš ʾet hā-ʾādām, with cherubim and a flaming sword guarding the tree of life: God drives the man out; Q 2:36 fa-akhrajahumā mimmā kānā fīhi: Satan is the subject who 'brought them out', then God's ihbiṭū 'go down' (2:36, 2:38), addressed to a plural. No cherubim, no tree of life. Gen 3:15 wĕ-ʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā û-bên hā-ʾiššâ û-bên zarʿăkā û-bên zarʿāh: enmity between serpent and woman and their offspring; Q 2:36 ihbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun: 'some of you enemies to others' among those sent down. The same decree of enmity (ʾêbâ / ʿaduww) at the expulsion, with the serpent gone. Gen 3:17-19 ʾărûrâ hā-ʾădāmâ baʿăbûrekā bĕ-ʿiṣṣābôn tōʾkălennâ ... ʿad šûbĕkā ʾel hā-ʾădāmâ: cursed ground, toil and death; Q 2:36 wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun wa-matāʿun ilā ḥīn: on earth an abode and provision for a time. The curses on ground, woman and serpent are left out; the earth is a lodging and a time limit, not a curse. The ending changes. Gen 3:12 hā-ʾiššâ ʾăšer nātattâ ʿimmādî hîʾ nātĕnâ-llî min hā-ʿēṣ wā-ʾōkēl: the man blames the woman (and God who gave her), with no repentance or pardon; Q 2:37 fa-talaqqā ādamu min rabbihi kalimātin fa-tāba ʿalayhi innahu huwa t-tawwābu r-raḥīm: Adam receives words and God turns to him in forgiveness before the descent. The Quran adds a reconciliation Genesis does not have.

Shared motifs, rarest first: The first man's response after the transgression in the garden (blame or repentance) [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The tempter in the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); Enmity decreed at the expulsion from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The human condition on earth after the expulsion [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); First humans expelled from the garden [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); God speaks in the plural (us, our) as if to a divine council (weight 6.0); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); A tree of knowledge whose fruit is forbidden (weight 5.8). Pair score 56.8.

Only in The serpent, the eating, the curses and the expulsion: Each accused shifts blame to another (man to woman, woman to serpent); First woman named as mother of all living; God heard walking in the garden in the breeze of the day; Humans gain divine knowledge and God fears they will also gain immortality; Woman punished with pain in childbirth and subordination to husband; The woman eats first and gives the fruit to her husband; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts]; Cherubim and a flaming turning sword guard the way to the tree of life; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts]; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God makes garments of skin for the first couple; God makes garments of skin for the first couple [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.

Only in Adam, the angels and Iblis: God teaches Adam all the names and he recites them to the angels, who cannot; The expelled are told 'Go down, enemies to one another' with a dwelling and provision on earth for a time; God announces to the angels he will place a vicegerent (khalifa) on earth; The first man names the animals; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; God speaks to heavenly beings about making man [divergence between the texts]; The office given to humans on earth at creation [divergence between the texts]; Whoever sheds human blood, by man shall his blood be shed, because humans bear God's image; and 4 more.

Gen: wəhannāḥāš hāyâ ʿārûm ... wayyōʾmer ʾel-hāʾiššâ, a clever beast addressing the woman. The serpent and the woman as first addressee drop out. What the tree offers. Gen: knowledge, wihyîtem kēʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôb wārāʿ; immortality belongs to a second tree that God guards, pen-yišlaḥ yādô wəlāqaḥ gam mēʿēṣ haḥayyîm wəʾākal wāḥay ləʿōlām. Q: the tempter names the forbidden tree itself shajarati l-khuldi wa-mulkin lā yablā. Gen's two trees merge into one, and the lure becomes eternal life and kingship, not godlike knowledge. wattōʾkal wattittēn gam-ləʾîšāh ... wayyōʾkal wattippāqaḥnâ ʿênê šənêhem wayyēdəʿû kî ʿêrummim hēm wayyitpərû ʿălēh təʾēnâ; fa-akalā minhā fa-badat lahumā sawʾātuhumā wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-janna. Changes: in Gen the woman eats first and hands it on, while Q has both eat and puts the blame on Adam (wa-ʿaṣā Ādamu rabbahu fa-ghawā); fig leaves become just 'leaves of the garden'. Gen goes from the eating straight to curses, ʾărûrâ hāʾădāmâ baʿăbûrekā ... kî-ʿāpār ʾattâ wəʾel-ʿāpār tāšûb, with no repentance and no forgiveness. Q puts election and forgiveness before the descent, thumma jtabāhu rabbuhu fa-tāba ʿalayhi wa-hadā. Adam's sin is forgiven, not cursed, and no death sentence follows. wəʾêbâ ʾāšît bênkā ûbên hāʾiššâ ûbên zarʿăkā ûbên zarʿāh ... wayəšalləḥēhû ... waygāreš ʾet-hāʾādām; qāla hbiṭā minhā jamīʿan baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduww. Enmity and expulsion. Gen's enmity is between serpent and woman and their seed, and the way back is barred by cherubim. Q's enmity is among those sent down, and Q adds a promise of guidance, fa-immā yaʾtiyannakum minnī hudan fa-mani ttabaʿa hudāya fa-lā yaḍillu wa-lā yashqā.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo, parallel. A different tempter. Gen: wə-han-nāḥāš hāyāh ʿārûm mik-kōl ḥayyat haś-śādeh, an animal speaking to the woman. Q: fa-waswasa lahumā l-shayṭānu, the devil already expelled in 7:13, whispering to both, and he swears an oath (wa-qāsamahumā innī lakumā la-mina l-nāṣiḥīna). There is no serpent and no curse to crawl on the belly (Gen 3:14). What the tempter promises. Gen: wi-hyîtem kē-ʾlōhîm yōdəʿê ṭôv wā-rāʿ, and God himself confirms the danger: hēn hā-ʾādām hāyāh kə-ʾaḥad mimmennû ... wā-ḥay lə-ʿōlām. Q: mā nahākumā rabbukumā ʿan hādhihi l-shajarati illā an takūnā malakayni aw takūnā mina l-khālidīna. 'Like gods knowing good and evil' becomes 'angels or immortals', a lie (bi-ghurūrin). Q has no divine admission that the humans have become 'like one of us'. Who is tempted and eats first. Gen: the serpent talks to the woman (wa-yyōʾmer ʾel-hā-ʾiššāh), she eats first and gives to her husband (wat-tittēn gam-lə-ʾîšāh ʿimmāh wa-yyōʾkhal). Q uses the dual throughout: wa-zawjuka ... fa-kulā ... wa-lā taqrabā ... waswasa lahumā ... fa-lammā dhāqā l-shajarata. The couple acts together and the woman is not singled out. Gen 3:3, the woman's paraphrase: wə-lōʾ tiggəʿû bô, 'nor touch it', a fence God had not said. Q, God's own command: wa-lā taqrabā hādhihi l-shajarata, 'do not come near'. The tree is unnamed in Q (no 'knowledge of good and evil'). Gen: wat-tippāqaḥnāh ʿênê šənêhem wa-yyēdəʿû kî ʿêrummim hēm wa-yyitpərû ʿălēh təʾēnāh. Q: badat lahumā sawʾātuhumā wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni ʿalayhimā min waraqi l-jannati. Both sew leaves, but in Q they are 'leaves of the garden' (no fig), and Q says the nakedness 'appeared' rather than 'their eyes were opened'. God's question. Gen: the couple hide (wa-yyitḥabbēʾ hā-ʾādām wə-ʾištô), God walks in the garden and calls ʾayyekkāh, then ha-min-hā-ʿēṣ ... ʾākhāltā. Q: wa-nādāhumā rabbuhumā a-lam anhakumā ʿan tilkumā l-shajarati wa-aqul lakumā inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduwwun mubīnun. No hiding and no walking God; the question is a reminder of a warning given.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 107 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: List of kings who reigned 'before any king reigned over the Israelites' (weight 6.7); A queen's ancestry includes a figure named 'Waters of Gold' (Me-Zahav) (weight 6.7); Lists of tribal chiefs (allufim) of Edom and the Horites (weight 6.7); King list in which each successor comes from a different city, not the son of his predecessor (weight 6.7); First king of Edom is Bela son of Beor (name recalling Balaam son of Beor) (weight 6.7); Ancient giant or Rephaite peoples (Rephaim, Zuzim, Emim, Horites) defeated (weight 5.1). Pair score 38.5.

Only in Generations of Esau, Horite chiefs, kings of Edom: Amalek's ancestor is born to a concubine in Esau's line; Brothers separate because the land cannot support both their herds; While herding his father's asses, a man discovers 'the yemim' in the wilderness (hot springs or mules).

Only in Sons of Ishmael, Keturah and Esau; the Seirite chiefs and kings of Edom: Abraham's sons by the concubine Keturah (Midian, Sheba, Dedan...); Ishmael promised to father twelve princes and a great nation; Ishmael's twelve sons as Arabian tribes (Nebaioth, Kedar, Dumah, Tema...); A lone daughter is named in a male genealogy (Dinah, Serah).

title: Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt ↔ Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read)

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. aḥada ʿashara kawkaban wa-sh-shamsa wa-l-qamara raʾaytuhum lī sājidīn; haššemeš wəhayyārēaḥ wəʾaḥad ʿāśār kôkābîm mištaḥăwîm lî: same eleven stars, sun and moon bowing. Q omits the first dream of the sheaves (Gen 37:7). Reversal of the father's response. Gen: Joseph tells father and brothers (wayəsappēr ʾel-ʾābîw wəʾel-ʾeḥāyw), and the father rebukes him (wayyigʿar-bô ʾābîw: hăbôʾ nābôʾ ʾănî wəʾimməkā ...?). Q: Joseph tells only his father, who warns 'lā taqṣuṣ ruʾyāka ʿalā ikhwatika fa-yakīdū laka kaydā' and interprets the dream as election: yajtabīka rabbuka wa-yuʿallimuka min taʾwīli l-aḥādīth. Gen: the narrator states it, wəyiśrāʾēl ʾāhab ʾet-yôsēp mikkol-bānāyw kî ben-zəqunîm, and gives the kətōnet passîm as its sign. Q: only the brothers say it, and of two sons: la-Yūsufu wa-akhūhu aḥabbu ilā abīnā minnā ... inna abānā la-fī ḍalālin mubīn. The coat as token of favoritism is dropped; the shirt (qamīṣ) returns only as evidence. Gen: ləkû wənahargēhû wənašlikēhû bəʾaḥad habbōrôt ... wənirʾeh mah-yyihyû ḥălōmōtāyw (to defeat the dreams). Q: uqtulū Yūsufa awi ṭraḥūhu arḍan yakhlu lakum wajhu abīkum wa-takūnū min baʿdihi qawman ṣāliḥīn: the motive is the father's face, and the plotters plan to become righteous afterwards. Gen names two brothers: Reuben (ʾal-tišpəkû-dām, hašlîkû ʾōtô ʾel-habbôr hazzeh, meaning to restore him) and Judah (mah-beṣaʿ ... ləkû wənimkərennû layyišməʿēʾlîm). Q leaves one speaker unnamed, qāʾilun minhum, and merges both: throw him into ghayābati l-jubb so that baʿḍu s-sayyāra will pick him up. Reversal of initiative. Gen: Israel himself sends Joseph, ləkâ wəʾešlāḥăkā ʾălêhem ... rəʾēh ʾet-šəlôm ʾaḥêkā. Q: the brothers ask (arsilhu maʿanā ghadan yartaʿ wa-yalʿab) and the father is reluctant: innī la-yaḥzununī an tadhhabū bihi.

Only in Joseph's dreams, the pit and the sale to Egypt: Brothers sit down to eat bread after casting their brother into the pit; Hero's story begins when he is seventeen; Young hero brings bad reports of his brothers to their father; An anonymous man finds the wandering hero in the field and directs him; Dream of the brothers' sheaves bowing to the hero's sheaf; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; Father himself sends the hero to his brothers; Evidence presented with the formula 'Please recognize (haker na)' whose is this; Father gives the hero a special garment; Called by name, the hero answers 'Here I am' (hineni).

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 88 more.

summary: These two units share 13 motifs: the woman falsely accuses the hero of assault [divergence between the texts], hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode [divergence between the texts], hero nearly yields but a sign from god stops him [divergence between the texts], hero thrown into prison [divergence between the texts]….

Q: the master finds both at the door (wa-alfayā sayyidahā ladā l-bāb), accepts the shirt-test of a witness min ahlihā, and blames her: innahu min kaydikunna inna kaydakunna ʿaẓīm ... wa-staghfirī li-dhanbiki. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. wayhî YHWH ʾet-yôsēp wayhî ʾîš maṣlîaḥ; wa-ka-dhālika makkannā li-Yūsufa fī l-arḍ ... ātaynāhu ḥukman wa-ʿilmā: God's favor rests on the slave. wa-rāwadathu llatī huwa fī baytihā ʿan nafsihi wa-ghallaqati l-abwāba wa-qālat hayta lak; wattiśśāʾ ʾēšet-ʾădōnāyw ʾet-ʿênêhā ... šikbâ ʿimmî, wəʾên ʾîš mēʾanšê habbayit šām: the master's wife, alone with him in the house. maʿādha llāhi innahu rabbī aḥsana mathwāy; hēn ʾădōnî lōʾ-yādaʿ ʾittî ... wəḥāṭāʾtî lēʾlōhîm: loyalty to the master and to God. Q's rabbī can mean either. Addition. Gen: Joseph refuses at once and every day, wayəmāʾēn ... wəlōʾ-šāmaʿ ʾēlêhā. Q: wa-la-qad hammat bihi wa-hamma bihā lawlā an raʾā burhāna rabbih: he was on the point of yielding, and only God's sign stops him. Reversal of what the garment proves. Gen: she seizes his garment (wattitpəśēhû bəbigdô), he leaves it in her hand, and she keeps it to accuse him (wattannaḥ bigdô ʾeṣlāh). Q: she tears his shirt from behind (qaddat qamīṣahu min dubur), and the tear clears him: in kāna qamīṣuhu qudda min dubur fa-kadhabat. Gen: the master believes his wife, wayyiḥar ʾappô, and jails Joseph at once. Q: the master finds both at the door (wa-alfayā sayyidahā ladā l-bāb), accepts the shirt-test of a witness min ahlihā, and blames her: innahu min kaydikunna inna kaydakunna ʿaẓīm ... wa-staghfirī li-dhanbiki. Gen's ʾîš ʿibrî ... ləṣaḥeq bānû (the foreign slave) is absent.

Only in Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison: The jailer puts all the prisoners in the hero's charge; God blesses a foreigner's house for the sake of the righteous slave; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 96 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God's favor rests on the hero while he is a slave or prisoner (weight 6.0); Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode (weight 6.0); Hero refuses, citing loyalty to his master and to God (weight 6.0); Seduction attempt when the two are alone in the house (weight 5.8); Hero thrown into prison (weight 5.8); The master's wife tries to seduce the hero (weight 5.8); The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault (weight 5.8); Hero bought by an Egyptian official (weight 5.8); Hero's beauty is remarked on (weight 4.9). Pair score 51.8.

Only in Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison: The jailer puts all the prisoners in the hero's charge; God blesses a foreigner's house for the sake of the righteous slave; The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault [divergence between the texts]; Hero's garment becomes evidence in the seduction episode [divergence between the texts]; Hero thrown into prison [divergence between the texts]; Hero nearly yields but a sign from God stops him [divergence between the texts]; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero.

Only in Joseph in the Quran (Surah 12): Brothers persuade the reluctant father to send the hero with them; Brothers come to their father at night, weeping; God reassures the hero in the pit; Hero reveals himself to the youngest brother first; Father does not believe the brothers' story; Father warns the hero not to tell his dream to his brothers; Hero's garment restores the father's sight; Hero refuses release until his innocence is established; Hero prays to die in submission and join the righteous; Hero preaches monotheism to his fellow prisoners; Hero prays that prison is preferable to sin; The husband recognizes his wife's guilt; and 48 more.

title: Cain and Abel ↔ The two sons of Adam, the raven, and whoever saves one life
summary: These two units share 7 motifs: god accepts one brother's offering and rejects the other's [divergence between the texts], what the earth does with the murdered brother: takes in his blood, or hides his corpse [divergence between the texts], a brother kills his brother in the first murder [divergence between the texts], the first murderer's lament after the deed [divergence between the texts]….

passages.note: God accepts one brother's offering and rejects the other's [divergence between the texts] (Gen names Qayin and Hevel, specifies the gifts (pərî hā-ʾădāmāh against bəkhōrôt ṣōʾnô û-mē-ḥelvēhen), and gives no reason for God's choice (wa-yyišaʿ ... lōʾ šāʿāh). Q: the brothers are unnamed (ibnay Ādama), the gifts unspecified (qarrabā qurbānan), and the reason is spoken by the victim: innamā yataqabbalu llāhu mina l-muttaqīna.)

Gen names Qayin and Hevel, specifies the gifts (pərî hā-ʾădāmāh against bəkhōrôt ṣōʾnô û-mē-ḥelvēhen), and gives no reason for God's choice (wa-yyišaʿ ... lōʾ šāʿāh). Q: the brothers are unnamed (ibnay Ādama), the gifts unspecified (qarrabā qurbānan), and the reason is spoken by the victim: innamā yataqabbalu llāhu mina l-muttaqīna. A change of speaker. In Gen, God warns Cain before the murder: lāmmāh ḥārāh lākh ... lap-petaḥ ḥaṭṭāʾt rōvēṣ wə-ʾēlêkhā təšûqātô wə-ʾattāh timšol-bô. In Q God is silent and the victim gives the warning: laʾin basaṭta ilayya yadaka ... mā ana bi-bāsiṭin yadiya ilayka ... innī akhāfu llāha rabba l-ʿālamīna. The crouching desire comes back as fa-ṭawwaʿat lahu nafsuhu qatla akhīhi. MT: wa-yyōʾmer Qayin ʾel-Hevel ʾāḥîw, with the speech missing, then wa-yyāqom ... wa-yyahargēhû. Q supplies the dialogue: qāla la-aqtulannaka, and Abel's reply. Then fa-qatalahu fa-aṣbaḥa mina l-khāsirīna. cf. (not a match) Targum Neofiti and Pseudo-Jonathan Gen 4:8, which also supply a dispute in the field. What the earth does differs. Gen: the ground opens its mouth to take the blood, and the blood cries out (qôl dəmê ʾāḥîkhā ṣōʿăqîm ʾēlay min-hā-ʾădāmāh ... ʾăšer pāṣətāh ʾet-pîhā), so the crime is exposed. Q: God sends a raven digging in the earth (ghurāban yabḥathu fī l-arḍi) to show how to hide (yuwārī) the brother's corpse (sawʾata akhīhi). Gen has no burial; Q has no interrogation ('ê Hevel), curse, wandering or mark. cf. (not a match) Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 21 (raven and burial). The murderer's lament. Gen: gādôl ʿăwōnî minnəśōʾ ... nāʿ wā-nād, a complaint about the punishment. Q: yā waylatā aʿajaztu an akūna mithla hādhā l-ghurābi fa-uwāriya sawʾata akhī fa-aṣbaḥa mina l-nādimīna, shame at being outdone by a raven, and remorse. Q has no punishment on earth; it ends in remorse.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. aʿṣiru khamran / aḥmilu fawqa raʾsī khubzan taʾkulu ṭ-ṭayru minh; wāʾeśḥaṭ ʾōtām ʾel-kôs parʿōh / šəlōšâ sallê ḥōrî ʿal-rōʾšî ... wəhāʿôp ʾōkēl ʾōtām. Q makes them two fatayān and drops their offices (śar hammašqîm, śar hāʾôpîm) and the three branches and baskets. Gen: one sentence, hălôʾ lēʾlōhîm pitrōnîm. Q: dhālikumā mimmā ʿallamanī rabbī, followed by a sermon added before the interpretation: millata ābāʾī Ibrāhīma wa-Isḥāqa wa-Yaʿqūb ... a-arbābun mutafarriqūna khayrun ami llāhu l-wāḥidu l-qahhār. The dream scene becomes a call to monotheism. fa-yasqī rabbahu khamran wa-ammā l-ākharu fa-yuṣlabu fa-taʾkulu ṭ-ṭayru min raʾsih; wətālâ ʾôtəkā ʿal-ʿēṣ wəʾākal hāʿôp ʾet-bəśārəkā. Q drops the three-day term and the pun yiśśāʾ parʿōh ʾet-rōʾšəkā. Gen: the cupbearer simply forgets, wəlōʾ-zākar ... wayyiškāḥēhû. Q names an agent, fa-ansāhu sh-shayṭānu dhikra rabbih (ambiguous: he forgot to mention Joseph to his master, or Joseph forgot his Lord). Gen's šənātayim yāmîm (41:1) becomes biḍʿa sinīn.

Shared motifs, rarest first: Hero attributes his dream interpretation to God [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The freed prisoner forgets the hero for years [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.7); The freed prisoner forgets the hero for years (weight 6.0); Birds eat bread from on top of the dreamer's head (weight 6.0); One prisoner is restored, the other executed and his body exposed (weight 6.0); Two fellow prisoners dream of pressing wine and carrying bread (weight 6.0); Hero asks the freed prisoner to mention him to the king (weight 6.0); Hero attributes his dream interpretation to God (weight 5.4). Pair score 48.8.

Only in The cupbearer's and baker's dreams: On the king's birthday feast prisoners are released or executed; 'Lift up your head' means restoration for one and beheading for the other; King's cupbearer and baker imprisoned for offending him; Three items in a dream (branches, baskets) signify three days; Pharaoh executes or threatens offenders by hanging, impaling or crucifixion.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 101 more.

evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, parallel. sabʿa baqarātin simānin yaʾkuluhunna sabʿun ʿijāfun wa-sabʿa sunbulātin khuḍrin wa-ukhara yābisāt; šebaʿ pārôt ... bərîʾōt bāśār / daqqôt bāśār; šebaʿ šibbŏlîm. The dreamer is al-malik in Q, not Pharaoh, although the Moses story in Q has Firʿawn. Gen: kol-ḥarṭummê miṣrayim ... wəʾên-pôtēr ʾôtām: they cannot interpret. evidence.text: Confirmed by a side-by-side reading of both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml): divergence, echo. fa-ʿarafahum wa-hum lahu munkirūn; wayyakkirēm wayyitnakkēr ʾălêhem ... wəhēm lōʾ hikkiruhû. Same root n-k-r on both sides, in opposite senses: in Gen Joseph makes himself strange (wayyitnakkēr), in Q the brothers fail to recognize him (munkirūn). Omission of the harshness. Gen: wayədabbēr ʾittām qāšôt, məraggəlîm ʾattem, three days in custody, one brother bound. Q: no spy charge. Joseph is a generous host, a-lā tarawna annī ūfī l-kayla wa-ana khayru l-munzilīn, and the only threat is fa-lā kayla lakum ʿindī. Reversed reaction. Gen: on finding the silver they are terrified, wayyēṣēʾ libbām wayyeḥerdû ... mah-zzōʾt ʿāśâ ʾĕlōhîm lānû. Q: they are glad, yā abānā mā nabghī hādhihi biḍāʿatunā ruddat ilaynā. Q also gives Joseph's motive, laʿallahum yarjiʿūn. Gen: grief and blame, ʾōtî šikkaltem ... lōʾ-yērēd bənî ʿimmākem ... wəhôradtem ʾet-śêbātî bəyāgôn šəʾôlâ. Q: hal āmanukum ʿalayhi illā ka-mā amintukum ʿalā akhīhi min qabl, fa-llāhu khayrun ḥāfiẓan: the father turns to trust in God. Gen: Joseph takes Simeon as hostage on the first journey, wayyiqqaḥ mēʾittām ʾet-šimʿôn wayyeʾĕsōr ʾōtô. Q: on the second journey the eldest stays of his own will after the cup affair, qāla kabīruhum ... fa-lan abraḥa l-arḍa ḥattā yaʾdhana lī abī.

Only in The brothers' first journey to Egypt: Hero speaks through an interpreter so the others do not know he understands them; Hero swears 'by the life of Pharaoh'; Brothers held in custody for three days; Brothers confess their old crime in front of the victim without knowing he hears them; Hero turns aside or withdraws to weep unseen before his brothers; Hero accuses his brothers of being spies; Father says losing his son will bring his grey hairs down to Sheol in sorrow; Famine forces the family to go down to Egypt.

Only in Joseph and his brothers (Surah 12, full read): Brothers tell their father to ask the town and the caravan to confirm their story; Brothers claim the accused youth's absent brother (the hero) had also stolen before; Famished brothers bring poor goods and ask the disguised hero for alms; The brothers confess 'we were sinners' once the hero is revealed and ask their father to pray for them; Father keeps lamenting his lost son for years until his sons fear he will waste away; The patriarch claims to know from God what his sons do not know; Father promises his repentant sons to ask God's forgiveness for them later; Fleeing the seductress, the hero and the woman find her husband at the door; The bereaved father answers with 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) and reliance on God; The hero could not have kept his brother under the king's law, so a stratagem is needed; The hero declares he follows the religion of his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; A camel-load is promised to whoever brings back the missing royal cup, with a guarantor; and 98 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Brothers come for grain and do not recognize the hero (weight 6.0); One brother stays behind in Egypt (weight 6.0); Their payment is secretly returned in their bags (weight 6.0); Hero demands they bring their youngest brother (weight 6.0); Family prostrates before the hero, fulfilling the dream (weight 5.8); A brother or the brothers give the father a pledge for the youngest (weight 5.8); Father refuses at first to send the youngest (weight 5.6). Pair score 41.1.

Only in The brothers' first journey to Egypt: Hero speaks through an interpreter so the others do not know he understands them; Hero swears 'by the life of Pharaoh'; Brothers held in custody for three days; Brothers confess their old crime in front of the victim without knowing he hears them; Father refuses at first to send the youngest [divergence between the texts]; Hero turns aside or withdraws to weep unseen before his brothers; Their payment is secretly returned in their bags [divergence between the texts]; One brother stays behind in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; Hero accuses his brothers of being spies; Hero accuses his brothers of being spies [divergence between the texts]; Father says losing his son will bring his grey hairs down to Sheol in sorrow; Famine forces the family to go down to Egypt.

Only in Joseph in the Quran (Surah 12): Brothers persuade the reluctant father to send the hero with them; Brothers come to their father at night, weeping; God reassures the hero in the pit; Hero reveals himself to the youngest brother first; Father does not believe the brothers' story; Father warns the hero not to tell his dream to his brothers; Hero's garment restores the father's sight; Hero refuses release until his innocence is established; Hero prays to die in submission and join the righteous; Hero preaches monotheism to his fellow prisoners; Hero prays that prison is preferable to sin; The husband recognizes his wife's guilt; and 50 more.
